title.zh: 卷九十七 列傳第五十七 夷蠻
title.raw: 卷九十七 列傳第五十七 夷蠻 Volume 97 Biographies 57: Yi Man

sentences.zh: 南夷、西南夷，大抵在交州之南及西南，居大海中洲上，相去或三五千里，遠者二三萬里，乘舶舉帆，道里不可詳知。

translations.literal: The southern Yi and southwestern Yi are mostly south and southwest of Jiaozhou, dwelling on islets in the great sea; distances between them are perhaps three to five thousand li, the farthest twenty or thirty thousand li; they travel by boat and raise sails—the routes and distances cannot be known in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The peoples of the southern and southwestern frontier lay for the most part south and southwest of Jiaozhou, on islands in the open sea. Some were separated by three to five thousand li, others by as much as twenty or thirty thousand li. They reached one another by ship under sail, and the exact courses and distances could not be fully charted.

sentences.zh: 外國諸夷雖言里數，非定實也。

translations.literal: Although the various foreign yi states state distances in li, these are not fixed facts.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign peoples gave figures in li, those numbers were not reliable measures.

sentences.zh: 南夷林邑國，高祖永初二年，林邑王范陽邁遣使貢獻，即加除授。

translations.literal: The southern-yi state of Linyi—in the second year of Yongchu under Emperor Gaozu, King Fanyang Mai of Linyi sent envoys with tribute and was immediately given appointment and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Among the southern peoples was the state of Linyi. In the second year of Yongchu (421), during the reign of Emperor Gaozu, King Fanyang Mai of Linyi sent envoys with tribute, and the court at once granted him titles and office.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉初，侵暴日南、九德諸郡，交州刺史杜弘文建牙聚眾欲討之，聞有代，乃止。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu, [Linyi] raided Rinan, Jiude, and other commanderies; Jiaozhou Inspector Du Hongwen raised his standard and gathered troops intending to attack, but hearing of a successor [to his post], he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wen, Linyi raided Rinan, Jiude, and neighboring commanderies. Jiaozhou inspector Du Hongwen mustered forces to campaign against them, but when he learned that his replacement was on the way, he abandoned the effort.

sentences.zh: 七年，陽邁遣使自陳與交州不睦，求蒙恕宥。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Yang Mai sent envoys stating on his own that relations with Jiaozhou were not peaceful and begging to be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (430), Yang Mai sent envoys explaining that he was at odds with Jiaozhou and asking for imperial clemency.

sentences.zh: 八年，又遣樓船百餘寇九德，入四會浦口，交州刺史阮彌之遣隊主相道生三千人赴討，攻區粟城不剋，引還。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, [Linyi] again sent over a hundred tower-ships to raid Jiude, entering the mouth of Sihui Inlet; Jiaozhou Inspector Ruan Mizhi sent company commander Xiang Daosheng with three thousand men to attack, failed to take Qu Su city, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Linyi sent more than a hundred warships against Jiude, entering Sihui harbor. Inspector Ruan Mizhi dispatched the company commander Xiang Daosheng with three thousand troops; they besieged Qu Su but could not take it and had to pull back.

sentences.zh: 林邑欲伐交州，借兵於扶南王，扶南不從。

translations.literal: Linyi wished to attack Jiaozhou and asked troops from the king of Funan; Funan did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: When Linyi planned to invade Jiaozhou, it asked Funan for troops, but the king of Funan refused.

sentences.zh: 十年，陽邁遣使上表獻方物，求領交州，詔答以道遠，不許。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Yang Mai sent envoys with a memorial presenting local products and requesting charge of Jiaozhou; an edict replied that the route was too distant and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (433), Yang Mai memorialized the throne with regional gifts and asked to be put in charge of Jiaozhou. The court answered that the distance was too great and declined.

sentences.zh: 十二、十五、十六、十八年，頻遣貢獻，而寇盜不已，所貢亦陋薄。

translations.literal: In the twelfth, fifteenth, sixteenth, and eighteenth years, [Linyi] repeatedly sent tribute, yet raiding did not cease, and what was offered was coarse and meager.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth, fifteenth, sixteenth, and eighteenth years envoys came again with tribute, but raids continued unabated and the gifts themselves were shabby.

sentences.zh: 太祖忿其違慠，二十三年，使龍驤將軍、交州刺史檀和之伐之，遣太尉府振武將軍宗慤受和之節度。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu resented their defiance and insolence; in the twenty-third year he sent Dragon Soaring General and Jiaozhou Inspector Tan Hezhi to attack them and dispatched Grand Marshal's Staff General Who Inspires Awe Zong Que to accept Hezhi's command.
translations.idiomatic: Infuriated by Linyi's defiance, Emperor Wen in the twenty-third year (446) ordered the Dragon Soaring General and Jiaozhou inspector Tan Hezhi to campaign against them, with Grand Marshal's staff officer Zong Que, General Who Inspires Awe, placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 和之遣府司馬蕭景憲為前鋒，慤仍領景憲軍副。

translations.literal: Hezhi sent his staff Major Xiao Jingxian as vanguard; Que still led Jingxian's army as second-in-command.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi appointed his staff major Xiao Jingxian to lead the van, while Zong Que served as his second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 陽邁聞將見討，遣使上表，求還所略日南民戶，奉獻國珍。

translations.literal: Yang Mai, hearing that he was to be attacked, sent envoys with a memorial asking to return the Rinan households he had seized and offering the state's treasures.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Mai learned that a punitive expedition was coming, he sent a memorial offering to restore the Rinan households he had carried off and to present the kingdom's treasures.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔和之：「陽邁果有款誠，許其歸順。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu instructed Hezhi: "If Yang Mai truly shows sincere intent, permit his submission."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen instructed Hezhi: "If Yang Mai proves sincere, you may accept his surrender."

sentences.zh: 其年二月，軍至朱梧戍，遣府戶曹參軍日南太守姜仲基、前部賊曹參軍蟜弘民隨傳詔畢願、高精奴等宣揚恩旨，陽邁執仲基、精奴等二十八人，遣弘民反命，外言歸款，猜防愈嚴。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year the army reached Zhuwu garrison and sent staff Registrar of Households and Administrator of Rinan Jiang Zhongji, former Senior Clerk for Banditry Jiao Hongmin, and with them the edict-bearers Bi Yuan, Gao Jingnu, and others to proclaim the gracious intent; Yang Mai seized Zhongji, Jingnu, and twenty-eight others, sent Hongmin back with a reply, outwardly spoke of submission, yet grew ever more suspicious and guarded.
translations.idiomatic: That second month the army reached Zhuwu garrison. Hezhi sent staff registrar and Rinan administrator Jiang Zhongji, together with former senior clerk for banditry Jiao Hongmin and the imperial messengers Bi Yuan and Gao Jingnu, to proclaim the court's gracious intent. Yang Mai seized Zhongji, Jingnu, and twenty-six others, sent Hongmin back with a reply, professed submission outwardly, and tightened his defenses all the more.

sentences.zh: 景憲等乃進軍向區粟城，陽邁遣大帥范扶龍大戍區粟，又遣水步軍徑至。

translations.literal: Jingxian and the others then advanced toward Qu Su city; Yang Mai sent the great commander Fan Fulong to garrison Qu Su heavily and also sent river and land forces directly there.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian then marched on Qu Su. Yang Mai sent his great commander Fan Fulong to hold the city in force and hurried additional land and river troops to its relief.

sentences.zh: 景憲破其外救，盡銳攻城，五月，剋之，斬扶龍大首，獲金銀雜物不可勝計。

translations.literal: Jingxian defeated their outer relief, concentrated elite forces to assault the city, and in the fifth month took it, beheading Fulong's head [chief], and capturing gold, silver, and miscellaneous goods beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian routed the relief force, threw his best troops into the assault, and in the fifth month took the city. Fan Fulong was beheaded, and the booty in gold, silver, and other goods was beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 乘勝追討，即剋林邑，陽邁父子並挺身奔逃，所獲珍異，皆是未名之寶。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in pursuit, they immediately took Linyi; Yang Mai, father and son, both fled in person; the rare treasures obtained were all gems without [prior] names.
translations.idiomatic: Following up the victory, they took Linyi itself. Yang Mai and his son fled for their lives. The exotic treasures seized were marvels the court had never before named.

sentences.zh: 上嘉將帥之功，詔曰：「林邑介恃遐險，久稽王誅。

translations.literal: The emperor praised the generals' achievement and issued an edict saying: "Linyi, relying on its distant perilous terrain, has long delayed the royal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his commanders and proclaimed: "Linyi, trusting in its remote and difficult terrain, has long escaped imperial punishment.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍、交州刺史檀和之忠果到列，思略經濟，禀命攻討，萬里推鋒，法命肅齊，文武畢力，潔己奉公，以身率下，故能立勳海外，震服殊俗。

translations.literal: Dragon Soaring General and Jiaozhou Inspector Tan Hezhi is loyal and resolute in the extreme, thoughtful in strategy and able in governance; receiving orders to attack, he pushed the spearhead ten thousand li, laws and commands were sternly unified, civil and military all exerted strength, he purified himself in serving the public and led subordinates by his person—therefore he could establish merit beyond the seas and awe distant peoples into submission.
translations.idiomatic: The Dragon Soaring General and Jiaozhou inspector Tan Hezhi has shown outstanding loyalty and resolution, sound strategy, and practical ability. Ordered to campaign, he drove his army ten thousand li; discipline held firm; civil and military officers gave their all; he kept himself pure in public service and led from the front. Thus he won glory beyond the seas and brought distant peoples to heel.

sentences.zh: 宜加褒飾，參管近侍，可黃門侍郎，領越騎校尉、行建武將軍。

translations.literal: He should receive added commendation and decoration, participate in managing the close attendants; he may be made Yellow Gate Gentleman-Attendant, holding the post of Colonel of the Yue Cavalry and acting as General Who Establishes Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: He is to be further honored and appointed to attend the inner court as Gentleman-Attendant at the Yellow Gate, while retaining his posts as Colonel of the Yue Cavalry and Acting General Who Establishes Martiality.

sentences.zh: 龍驤司馬蕭景憲協贊軍首，勤捷顯著，總勒前驅，剋殄巢穴，必能威服荒夷，撫懷民庶。

translations.literal: Dragon Soaring Major Xiao Jingxian assisted and praised the army head, his diligence and swiftness were conspicuous, he commanded the vanguard, destroyed the nest and lair, and will surely be able to awe the wild yi into submission and comfort the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The Dragon Soaring major Xiao Jingxian aided the commander with conspicuous energy and skill, led the van, and destroyed the enemy stronghold. He is sure to overawe the frontier peoples and win the hearts of the populace.

sentences.zh: 可持節、督交州廣州之鬱林寧浦二郡諸軍事、建威將軍、交州刺史。」

translations.literal: He may bear the staff of authority, supervise all military affairs of the two commanderies Yulin and Ningpu in Jiaozhou and Guangzhou, be General Who Establishes Might, and Jiaozhou Inspector."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Jiaozhou and Guangzhou for the Yulin and Ningpu commanderies, General Who Establishes Might, and Inspector of Jiaozhou."

sentences.zh: 龍驤司馬童林之、九真太守傅蔚祖戰死，並贈給事中。

translations.literal: Dragon Soaring Major Tong Linzhi and Administrator of Jiuzhen Fu Weizu died in battle; both were posthumously given the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Dragon Soaring major Tong Linzhi and Jiuzhen administrator Fu Weizu fell in battle; both were posthumously made Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝建二年，林邑又遣長史范龍跋奉使貢獻，除龍跋揚武將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Shizu, Linyi again sent Chief Clerk Fan Longba as envoy with tribute; Longba was appointed General Who Displays Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian (455), under Emperor Xiaowu, Linyi again sent its chief clerk Fan Longba with tribute. Longba was made General Who Displays Martiality.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，林邑王范神成又遣長史范流奉表獻金銀器及香布諸物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, King Fanshencheng of Linyi again sent Chief Clerk Fan Liu with a memorial presenting gold and silver vessels, fragrant cloth, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming (458), King Fanshencheng of Linyi sent his chief clerk Fan Liu with a memorial offering gold and silver vessels, scented cloth, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰豫元年，又遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiyu under Emperor Taizong, [Linyi] again sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiyu (472), under Emperor Ming, envoys came again with regional gifts.

sentences.zh: 初，檀和之被徵至豫章，值豫章民胡誕世等反，因討平之，并論林邑功，封雲杜縣子，食邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tan Hezhi was summoned to Yuzhang, the people of Yuzhang, Hu Danshi and others, rebelled; he therefore attacked and pacified them, and together with accounting the Linyi achievement, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yundu with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Tan Hezhi was being recalled to Yuzhang, the Yuzhang native Hu Danshi and others rose in revolt. He suppressed them and, on the strength of his Linyi campaign as well, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yundu with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 和之，高平金鄉人，檀憑子也。

translations.literal: Hezhi was a man of Jinxiang in Gaoping, son of Tan Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping commandery and the son of Tan Ping.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉二十七年，自太子左衞率為世祖鎮軍司馬、輔國將軍、彭城太守。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu, from Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard he became Staff Major to the Pacifying Army of Shizu, General Who Assists the State, and Administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia (450), he moved from Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard to become staff major to the heir apparent's Pacifying Army, General Who Assists the State, and administrator of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，以為西中郎將、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When the arch-culprit [Liu Shao] murdered and usurped the throne, [Hezhi] was made General of the Right of the Center and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed crown prince Liu Shao murdered his father and seized the throne, Hezhi was appointed General of the Right of the Center and inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: [1]世祖入討，加輔國將軍，統豫州戍事，因出南奔。

translations.literal: [1] When Shizu entered to attack [the usurper], [Hezhi] was promoted to General Who Assists the State, commanded Yongzhou garrison affairs, and therefore fled south.
translations.idiomatic: [1] When the future Emperor Xiaowu marched north against the usurper, Hezhi was promoted to General Who Assists the State and put in charge of Yongzhou's garrison, but he fled south instead.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，以為右衞將軍。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, [Hezhi] was made General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaowu succeeded, Hezhi was made General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，除輔國將軍、豫州刺史，不行，復為右衞，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he was dismissed as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yuzhou, did not take office, and again became Right Guard, with added title Attendant Cavalier at Large.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian (455) he was appointed General Who Assists the State and inspector of Yuzhou but declined the post, returning instead to the Right Guard with the additional title of Attendant Cavalier at Large.

sentences.zh: 三年，出為南兗州刺史，坐酣飲黷貨，迎獄中女子入內，免官禁錮。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out as Inspector of Southern Yanzhou; for drunkenness, corrupt taking of goods, and bringing a woman from prison into his inner quarters, he was removed from office and confined.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent out as inspector of Southern Yanzhou. He was dismissed and placed under house arrest for habitual drunkenness, taking bribes, and bringing a woman from prison into his private quarters.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，追贈左將軍，諡曰襄子。

translations.literal: That year he died; posthumously he was given General of the Left; his posthumous title was Viscount Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same year and was posthumously made General of the Left with the posthumous title Viscount Xiang.

sentences.zh: 廣州諸山並俚、獠，種類繁熾，前後屢為侵暴，歷世患苦之。

translations.literal: The mountains of Guangzhou were all Li and Liao [peoples]; their kinds were numerous and flourishing; before and after they repeatedly committed invasions and violence, and successive generations suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: The hill country of Guangzhou was home to Li and Liao peoples in great variety and numbers. Generation after generation they raided the lowlands, and the region had long groaned under their attacks.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明中，合浦大帥陳檀歸順，拜龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: In the Daming era under Emperor Shizu, the great commander of Hepu, Chen Tan, submitted; he was appointed Dragon Soaring General.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming era under Emperor Xiaowu, Chen Tan, a great chieftain of Hepu, submitted to the court and was made Dragon Soaring General.

sentences.zh: 四年，檀表乞官軍征討未附，乃以檀為高興太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Tan memorialized begging that government troops campaign against those not yet attached; Tan was then made Administrator of Gaoxing, his generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (460) Chen Tan asked that imperial troops subdue those who had not yet submitted. He was appointed administrator of Gaoxing while retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 遣前朱提太守費沈、龍驤將軍武期率眾南伐，并通朱崖道，並無功，輒殺檀而反，沈下獄死。

translations.literal: The former Administrator of Zhuti Fei Shen and Dragon Soaring General Wu Qi were sent leading troops south to attack, and also to open the Zhuya route; all achieved nothing; they promptly killed Tan and rebelled; Shen was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent the former Zhuti administrator Fei Shen and the Dragon Soaring general Wu Qi south with an army, also to open the route to Zhuya. They accomplished nothing, murdered Chen Tan, and rebelled. Shen was thrown into prison and died there.

sentences.zh: 扶南國，太祖元嘉十一、十二、十五年，國王持黎跋摩遣使奉獻。

translations.literal: The state of Funan—in the eleventh, twelfth, and fifteenth years of Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu, King Jayavarman sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Funan sent tribute in the eleventh, twelfth, and fifteenth years of Yuanjia (434–438), when King Jayavarman dispatched envoys to Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 西南夷訶羅陁國，元嘉七年，遣使奉表曰：

translations.literal: The southwestern-yi state of Heluoduo—in the seventh year of Yuanjia sent envoys with a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Among the southwestern peoples was the state of Heluoduo. In the seventh year of Yuanjia (430) it sent envoys with a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 伏承聖主，信重三寶，興立塔寺，周滿國界。

translations.literal: I bow and receive [news of] the sage lord who trusts and honors the Three Treasures, raises towers and temples, filling the whole realm's borders.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that the sage sovereign honors the Three Treasures, raises stupas and temples, and fills the land with them.

sentences.zh: 城郭莊嚴，清淨無穢，四衢交通，廣博平坦。

translations.literal: City walls and suburbs are solemn, pure and without defilement; the four thoroughfares connect, broad and level.
translations.idiomatic: Your cities are majestic and pure, your crossroads broad and level.

sentences.zh: 臺殿羅列，狀若眾山，莊嚴微妙，猶如天宮。

translations.literal: Terraces and halls stand in rows like many mountains, solemn and subtle, like a heavenly palace.
translations.idiomatic: Terraces and halls stand in ranks like mountain ranges, refined and splendid as a palace of heaven.

sentences.zh: 聖王出時，四兵具足，導從無數，以為守衞。

translations.literal: When the sage king goes forth, the four armies are complete, guides and followers beyond number serve as guards.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacred king goes abroad, the four armies are complete and countless attendants guard him.

sentences.zh: 都人士女，麗服光飾，市廛豐富，珍賄無量，王法清整，無相侵奪。

translations.literal: Capital gentlemen and ladies wear beautiful robes and shining adornments; markets are rich, precious gifts without limit; royal law is pure and ordered, without mutual seizure and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women of the capital dress in splendor; the markets overflow with goods and treasure; your laws are just, and none plunder one another.

sentences.zh: 學徒遊集，三乘競進，敷演正法，雲布雨潤。

translations.literal: Students and disciples gather and roam; the three vehicles vie in advance; the true Dharma is spread and performed, like clouds deployed and rain moistening.
translations.idiomatic: Students gather everywhere; the three vehicles advance together; the true Dharma spreads like clouds and rain.

sentences.zh: 四海流通，萬國交會，長江眇漫，清淨深廣，有生咸資，莫能銷穢，陰陽調和，災厲不行。

translations.literal: Within the four seas there is circulation; ten thousand states meet; the Long River is vast, pure, deep, and broad; all living beings are provided for, none can consume defilement; yin and yang are harmonized; pestilence does not occur.
translations.idiomatic: The four seas are open and all nations meet; the Yangzi flows pure, deep, and wide, sustaining every living thing; yin and yang are in harmony and no plague walks the land.

sentences.zh: 誰有斯美，大宋揚都，聖王無倫，臨覆上國。

translations.literal: Who has such beauty? Great Song, Yangdu—sage king without peer, overlooking and covering the upper realm.
translations.idiomatic: Who else possesses such glory? Great Song at Yangdu—your sacred king is without equal, ruling the upper realm.

sentences.zh: 有大慈悲，子育萬物，平等忍辱，怨親無二，濟乏周窮，無所藏積，靡不照達，如日之明，無不受樂，猶如淨月。

translations.literal: He has great compassion, nurturing the ten thousand things as children; equal patience and forbearance, foe and kin without duality; relieving the lacking and surrounding the destitute, nothing hoarded in store; nothing not illuminated and reached, like the sun's brightness; none not receiving joy, like the pure moon.
translations.idiomatic: You are filled with compassion, nurturing all beings as a parent; you bear insult with equanimity and make no distinction between friend and foe; you relieve the poor and keep nothing in store; your light reaches everywhere like the sun; all rejoice in you as under a clear moon.

sentences.zh: 宰輔賢良，羣臣貞潔，盡忠奉主，心無異想。

translations.literal: Chancellors and assistants are worthy and good; the host of ministers are chaste and pure, all loyal in serving the lord, minds without other thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Your ministers are worthy; your officials upright; all serve the throne with undivided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝，是我真主。

translations.literal: I bow and consider: the emperor is my true lord.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before the emperor, who is my true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 臣是訶羅陁國王名曰堅鎧，今敬稽首聖王足下，惟願大王知我此心久矣，非適今也。

translations.literal: Your subject is the king of Heluoduo, named Jiankai; now I respectfully bow my head at the sage king's feet; I only wish the great king to know that this heart of mine is long-standing, not only of today.
translations.idiomatic: I am Jiankai, king of Heluoduo. I bow my head at your feet and beg Your Majesty to know that this devotion is of long standing, not a sudden whim.

sentences.zh: 山海阻遠，無緣自達，今故遣使，表此丹誠。

translations.literal: Mountains and seas block and distance; I had no means to reach you myself; now I therefore send envoys to express this cinnabar sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and seas lie between us, and I could not come myself; I send these envoys to lay my loyal heart before you.

sentences.zh: 所遣二人，一名毗紉，一名婆田，令到天子足下。

translations.literal: The two persons sent are named Birin and Botian, ordered to reach the Son of Heaven's feet.
translations.idiomatic: The two men I send are named Birin and Botian; I charge them to come before the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 堅鎧微蔑，誰能知者，是故今遣二人，表此微心，此情既果，雖死猶生。

translations.literal: Jiankai is slight and mean—who can know [me]? Therefore I now send these two men to express this slight heart; if this feeling bears fruit, though I die it is as living.
translations.idiomatic: I am humble and obscure—who would know my mind? I send these two men to speak for me. If this plea succeeds, I shall count myself alive though I die.

sentences.zh: 仰惟大國，藩守曠遠，我即邊方藩守之一。

translations.literal: Looking up to consider the great state: frontier guards are vast and distant; I am one of the frontier guards on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Your great realm extends its protection far abroad; I am but one frontier guardian on its edge.

sentences.zh: 上國臣民，普蒙慈澤，願垂恩逮，等彼僕臣。

translations.literal: The upper realm's subjects and people all receive gracious favor; I wish grace extended to reach [us], equal to those servant subjects.
translations.idiomatic: All who dwell in your realm enjoy your kindness; extend that grace to us as to your own servants.

sentences.zh: 臣國先時人眾殷盛，不為諸國所見陵迫，今轉衰弱，鄰國競侵。

translations.literal: My state formerly had a flourishing population and was not seen by other states as subject to bullying and pressure; now it turns weak and declining, neighboring states competing in invasion.
translations.idiomatic: My kingdom was once populous and strong and suffered no bullying from its neighbors; now we grow weak and neighboring states press in on every side.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖王，遠垂覆護，并市易往反，不為禁閉。

translations.literal: I bow and wish the sage king to extend protection from afar, and also that trade go back and forth without being shut and barred.
translations.idiomatic: I beg the sacred king to shelter us from afar and to let merchants travel freely without hindrance.

sentences.zh: 若見哀念，願時遣還，令此諸國，不見輕侮，亦令大王名聲普聞，扶危救弱，正是今日。

translations.literal: If you show pity and remembrance, I wish you promptly to send [envoys] back, causing these various states not to see [us] lightly insulted, and also causing the great king's fame to be universally heard; supporting the endangered and saving the weak is precisely today.
translations.idiomatic: If you take pity on us, send your envoys back in good time so that these kingdoms will not despise us, and so that your renown may spread abroad—for today is the day to succor the weak.

sentences.zh: 今遣二人，是臣同心，有所宣啟，誠實可信。

translations.literal: The two men sent now are of one heart with your subject; whatever they declare and open forth is sincere and may be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: The two men I now send share my inmost heart; whatever they report is honest and may be believed.

sentences.zh: 願勑廣州時遣舶還，不令所在有所陵奪。

translations.literal: I wish you to order Guangzhou from time to time to send ships back, not allowing wherever they are to have seizure and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you instruct Guangzhou to send ships back regularly and forbid anyone along the route to rob or plunder them.

sentences.zh: 願自今以後，賜年年奉使。

translations.literal: I wish from now onward to be granted yearly tribute envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Grant us hereafter the right to send tribute envoys every year.

sentences.zh: 今奉微物，願垂哀納。

translations.literal: Now I present slight goods; I wish you to extend pity and accept.
translations.idiomatic: I now offer these humble gifts and beg you graciously to receive them.

sentences.zh: 呵羅單國治闍婆洲。

translations.literal: The state of Heluodan rules Java.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Heluodan ruled Java.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年，遣使獻金剛指鐶、赤鸚鵡鳥、天竺國白疊古貝、葉波國古貝等物。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia [it] sent envoys presenting diamond finger-rings, red parrots, white stacked ancient shell currency of Tianzhu, ancient shell currency of Yabo, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanjia (430) it sent envoys with diamond finger-rings, red parrots, white cotton cloth from India, ancient shell currency from Lambaka, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 十年，呵羅單國王毗沙跋摩奉表曰：

translations.literal: In the tenth year, King Vishnuvarman of Heluodan presented a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (433) King Vishnuvarman of Heluodan sent a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 常勝天子陛下：諸佛世尊，常樂安隱，三達六通，為世間道，是名如來，應供正覺，遺形舍利，造諸塔像，莊嚴國土，如須彌山，村邑聚落，次第羅匝，城郭館宇，如忉利天宮，宮殿高廣，樓閣莊嚴，四兵具足，能伏怨敵，國土豐樂，無諸患難。

translations.literal: Ever-Victorious Son of Heaven, Your Majesty: the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, ever delight in peace and ease, possess the three penetrations and six superknowledges, are the world's path—this is called Tathagata, Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Enlightened; relics of the departed form, building towers and images, adorning the realm like Mount Sumeru; villages and hamlets, settlements in successive encirclement; city walls and lodges like Trayastrimsha Heaven; palaces high and broad, towers and pavilions solemn; the four armies complete, able to subdue hostile enemies; the realm rich and joyful, without various calamities.
translations.idiomatic: To the Ever-Victorious Son of Heaven: the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, abide in peace; possessed of the three penetrations and six superknowledges, they are the path for the world—the Tathagata, worthy of offerings, perfectly enlightened. Their relics remain; stupas and images adorn your realm like Mount Sumeru. Villages and towns lie in ordered rings; your walls and halls are like the palace of Trayastrimsha Heaven—lofty palaces and solemn towers. The four armies stand complete and subdue every foe; the land is rich and at ease, free from every ill.

sentences.zh: 奉承先王，正法治化，人民良善，慶無不利，處雪山陰，雪水流注，百川洋溢，八味清淨，周匝屈曲，順趣大海，一切眾生，咸得受用。

translations.literal: Receiving and upholding the former kings, governing by correct law, the people are good and kind, rejoicing without nothing unbeneficial; situated on the snowy mountain's northern slope, snow waters flow and pour, the hundred streams overflow, eight flavors pure and clean, winding round in curves, complying toward the great sea—all living beings alike obtain use and enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: Following your forefathers, you rule by righteous law; your people are good and prosper in all they do. North of the snowy mountains snowmelt pours forth; a hundred streams swell, pure of the eight flavors, winding round till they reach the sea—and every creature drinks its fill.

sentences.zh: 於諸國土，殊勝第一，是名震旦，大宋揚都，承嗣常勝大王之業，德合天心，仁廕四海，聖智周備，化無不順，雖人是天，護世降生，功德寶藏，大悲救世，為我尊主常勝天子。

translations.literal: Among all states and lands, preeminent and first—this is called Zhendan; Great Song, Yangdu, inheriting the Ever-Victorious Great King's enterprise; virtue matching Heaven's heart, benevolence shading the four seas; sage wisdom complete in every part, transformation without what does not comply; though human yet heavenly, born to protect the world; treasure-store of merit, great compassion saving the world—my honored lord, the Ever-Victorious Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Among all lands you are supreme—this is China, Great Song at Yangdu. You inherit the work of the Ever-Victorious King; your virtue accords with Heaven, your kindness shades the four seas; your wisdom is complete and your transforming power obeys none. Though human, you are heaven-born to guard the world—a treasury of merit, great compassion saving all—and you are my lord, the Ever-Victorious Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 是故至誠五體敬禮。

translations.literal: Therefore with utmost sincerity I bow with the five limbs in respect.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I bow my whole body in deepest reverence.

sentences.zh: 呵羅單國王毗沙跋摩稽首問訊。

translations.literal: King Vishnuvarman of Heluodan bows his head in inquiry after your welfare.
translations.idiomatic: King Vishnuvarman of Heluodan bows his head and sends greeting.

sentences.zh: 其後為子所篡奪。

translations.literal: Afterward [the throne] was usurped by his son.
translations.idiomatic: Later his son seized the throne from him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又上表曰：

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, [he] again presented a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (436) he sent another memorial:

sentences.zh: 大吉天子足下：離淫怒癡，哀愍羣生，想好具足，天龍神等，恭敬供養，世尊威德，身光明照，如水中月，如日初出，眉間白豪，[2]普照十方，其白如雪，亦如月光，清淨如華，顏色照曜，威儀殊勝，諸天龍神之所恭敬，以正法寶，梵行眾僧，莊嚴國土，人民熾盛，安隱快樂。

translations.literal: At the feet of the Great-Auspice Son of Heaven: apart from lust, anger, and delusion; pitying and cherishing all beings; good thoughts complete in fullness; dragons of heaven and spirits and others respectfully offering and sustaining; the World-Honored One's majestic virtue, body light illuminating, like the moon in water, like the sun first rising; the white tuft between the brows [2] universally illuminating the ten directions, its whiteness like snow, also like moonlight, pure as a flower, countenance shining, majestic bearing extraordinary—the respect of all heaven-dragons and spirits; with the treasure of the true Dharma, Brahma-conduct host of monks, adorning the realm; the people flourishing and abundant, peaceful, secure, and joyful.
translations.idiomatic: At the feet of the Great-Auspice Son of Heaven: you are free of lust, anger, and delusion; you pity all beings; your good thoughts are complete. Dragons of heaven and spirits honor and serve you. The World-Honored One's majestic radiance shines upon you like the moon in water, like the sun at dawn; the white tuft between your brows [2] illumines the ten directions, white as snow, bright as the moon, pure as a flower. Your bearing is sublime; heaven's dragons and spirits bow before you. The treasure of the true Dharma and the monks in pure conduct adorn your realm; your people flourish in peace and joy.

sentences.zh: 城閣高峻，如乾他山，眾多勇士，守護此城，樓閣莊嚴，道巷平正，著種種衣，猶如天服，於一切國，為最殊勝吉。

translations.literal: City towers high and steep, like Mount Gandhara; numerous brave warriors guard this city; towers and pavilions solemn; streets and lanes level and straight; wearing various kinds of robes, like heavenly garments; among all states, the most extraordinary and auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Your walls rise high as Mount Gandhara; many brave warriors guard your city; your towers are solemn and your streets level. Your people wear every kind of robe like the garments of heaven. Among all kingdoms yours is the most sublime and blessed.

sentences.zh: 揚州城無憂天主，愍念羣生，安樂民人，律儀清淨，慈心深廣，正法治化，共養三寶，名稱遠至，一切並聞。

translations.literal: Yangzhou city—the Carefree Heaven Lord—pitying and remembering all beings, giving peace and joy to the people; discipline and rites pure and clean; compassionate mind deep and broad; governing and transforming by correct law; together sustaining the Three Treasures; fame reaching far; all alike hear.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangzhou—the Carefree Heaven Lord—you pity all beings and give your people peace and joy. Your discipline is pure, your compassion deep and wide; you rule by righteous law and honor the Three Treasures. Your fame has reached the farthest lands; all have heard of you.

sentences.zh: 民人樂見，如月初生，譬如梵王，世界之主，一切人天，恭敬作禮。

translations.literal: The people rejoice to see [you], like the moon newly risen; like Brahma King, lord of the world; all humans and gods respectfully perform obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Your people rejoice to behold you as at the new moon; like Brahma, lord of the world, all men and gods bow before you.

sentences.zh: 呵羅單跋摩以頂禮足，猶如現前，以體布地，如殿陛道，供養恭敬，如奉世尊，以頂著地，曲躬問訊。

translations.literal: Heluodan Bamo bows with the crown at the feet, as though present before [you]; spreads his body on the ground like palace steps and paths; offers and sustains with respect, as serving the World-Honored One; places the crown on the ground, bends the body in inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: I, Bamo of Heluodan, bow with my head at your feet as though you stood before me; I prostrate my body on the ground like the steps of your hall; I honor you as I would the World-Honored One, my head on the earth, my body bent in greeting.

sentences.zh: 忝承先業，嘉慶無量，忽為惡子所見爭奪，遂失本國。

translations.literal: I humbly inherit the former enterprise, boundless good fortune—suddenly the wicked son saw [fit] to contend and seize, and I thus lost my original state.
translations.idiomatic: I had the good fortune to inherit my father's realm—then a wicked son rose against me and I lost my kingdom.

sentences.zh: 今唯一心歸誠天子，以自存命。

translations.literal: Now with single mind I return in sincerity to the Son of Heaven to preserve my own life.
translations.idiomatic: Now I turn with all my heart to the Son of Heaven to preserve my life.

sentences.zh: 今遣毗紉問訊大家，意欲自往，歸誠宣訴，復畏大海，風波不達。

translations.literal: Now I send Birin to inquire after the great household; I wished to go myself to return in sincerity and declare and appeal, yet I fear the great sea—wind and waves do not allow reaching.
translations.idiomatic: I send Birin to greet you, great lord. I wished to come myself to lay my case before you, but I fear the sea and its storms and cannot reach you.

sentences.zh: 今命得存，亦由毗紉此人忠志，其恩難報。

translations.literal: That my life is now preserved is also because of this man Birin's loyal intent; his grace is hard to repay.
translations.idiomatic: That I still live is thanks to Birin's loyal devotion—a debt I can scarcely repay.

sentences.zh: 此是大家國，今為惡子所奪，而見驅擯，意頗忿惋，規欲雪復。

translations.literal: This is the great household's state; now the wicked son has seized it, and I am seen driven and expelled; my mind is rather resentful and grieved; I plan to wash away [the wrong] in revenge.
translations.idiomatic: This was your great realm's ally; a wicked son has seized it and driven me out. I burn with resentment and mean to take revenge.

sentences.zh: 伏願大家聽毗紉買諸鎧仗袍襖及馬，願為料理毗紉使得時還。

translations.literal: I bow and wish the great household to permit Birin to buy various armor, weapons, robes, padded coats, and horses; I wish you to arrange matters so Birin can return in good time.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, great lord, to let Birin purchase armor, weapons, robes, coats, and horses, and to see that he returns safely and soon.

sentences.zh: 前遣闍邪仙婆羅訶，蒙大家厚賜，悉惡子奪去，啟大家使知。

translations.literal: Previously I sent Jyotishipala; I received the great household's generous gifts—all were seized by the wicked son; I inform the great household so you may know.
translations.idiomatic: I once sent Jyotishipala and received your generous gifts, but the wicked son seized them all. I write so that you may know.

sentences.zh: 今奉薄獻，願垂納受。

translations.literal: Now I present a slight offering; I wish you to extend [favor] and accept.
translations.idiomatic: I now offer these humble gifts and beg you to accept them.

sentences.zh: 此後又遣使。

translations.literal: After this [Heluodan] again sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Heluodan sent envoys again.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，太祖詔曰：「訶羅單、媻皇、媻達三國，頻越遐海，款化納貢，遠誠宜甄，可並加除授。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Emperor Taizu issued an edict: "The three states Heluodan, Panhuang, and Panta have repeatedly crossed the distant sea, sincerely submitting and offering tribute; distant sincerity should be distinguished; all may jointly receive appointment and rank."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year (449) Emperor Wen proclaimed: "The three states Heluodan, Panhuang, and Panta have repeatedly crossed the distant seas with sincere submission and tribute. Their distant loyalty deserves reward; let them all be granted titles and office."

sentences.zh: 乃遣使策命之曰：「惟爾慕義款化，效誠荒遐，恩之所洽，殊遠必甄，用敷典章，顯茲策授。

translations.literal: Envoys were then sent with patent of appointment saying: "Only you, admiring righteousness and sincerely submitting, show loyalty in the wild and distant; where grace reaches, the extraordinarily far must be distinguished; therefore the canonical regulations are spread forth, displaying this patent appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were dispatched with patents of appointment: "You who admire righteousness and submit in sincerity, showing loyalty from the far frontier—where imperial grace reaches, even the remotest shall be honored. We therefore bestow these canonical titles upon you.

sentences.zh: 爾其欽奉凝命，永固厥職，可不慎歟。」

translations.literal: You shall respectfully receive and uphold the solemn command, forever securing your posts—is this not to be heeded?"
translations.idiomatic: Receive this solemn charge with reverence and hold your offices firm—can you do otherwise?"

sentences.zh: 二十九年，又遣長史媻和沙彌獻方物。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, [Panhuang] again sent Chief Clerk Panhe Shami presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (452) it again sent its chief clerk Panhe Shami with regional gifts.

sentences.zh: 媻皇國，元嘉二十六年，國王舍利媻羅跋摩遣使獻方物四十一種，太祖策命之為媻皇國王曰：「惟爾仰政邊城，率貢來庭，皇澤凱被，無幽不洽。

translations.literal: The state of Panhuang—in the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, King Shilipanluobamo sent envoys presenting forty-one kinds of local products; Emperor Taizu with patent of appointment made him King of Panhuang, saying: "Only you, looking up to governance at the border city, leading tribute to come to court—imperial grace triumphant and spread, none in the dark not harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Panhuang: in the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia (449) King Shilipanluobamo sent envoys with forty-one kinds of tribute. Emperor Wen invested him as King of Panhuang with a patent reading: "You who govern the frontier and lead your people to court—imperial grace spreads everywhere, even to the darkest corners.

sentences.zh: 宜班典策，授茲嘉命。

translations.literal: It is fitting to distribute the canonical patent and confer this fine command.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to issue this canonical patent and grant you this honorable charge.

sentences.zh: 爾其祗順禮度，式保厥終，可不慎歟。」

translations.literal: You shall respectfully comply with ritual norms and thereby secure your end—is this not to be heeded?"
translations.idiomatic: Obey the rites and preserve your realm to the end—can you do otherwise?"

sentences.zh: 二十八年，復貢獻。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, [Panhuang] again offered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (451) tribute came again.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝建三年，又遣長史竺那媻智奉表獻方物。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian under Emperor Shizu, [Panhuang] again sent Chief Clerk Zhuna Panzhi with a memorial presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian (456), under Emperor Xiaowu, it again sent its chief clerk Zhuna Panzhi with a memorial and gifts.

sentences.zh: 以那媻智為振威將軍。

translations.literal: Zhunapanzhi was appointed General Who Quells Might.
translations.idiomatic: Zhunapanzhi was made General Who Quells Might.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，獻赤白鸚鵡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming, [Panhuang] presented red and white parrots.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daming (459) it presented red and white parrots.

sentences.zh: 大明八年、太宗泰始二年，又遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daming and the second year of Taishi under Emperor Taizong, [Panhuang] again sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Daming (464) and the second year of Taishi (466), under Emperor Ming, tribute envoys came again.

sentences.zh: 太宗以其長史竺須羅達、前長史振威將軍竺那媻智並為龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong made its chief clerk Zhuxuliluoda and its former chief clerk, General Who Quells Might Zhuna Panzhi, both Dragon Soaring Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming appointed its chief clerk Zhuxuliluoda and its former chief clerk Zhuna Panzhi, General Who Quells Might, both as Dragon Soaring Generals.

sentences.zh: 媻達國，元嘉二十六年，國王舍利不陵伽跋摩遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: The state of Panta—in the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, King Shilibulingjiabamo sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Panta: in the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia (449) King Shilibulingjiabamo sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 太祖策命之為婆達國王曰：「惟爾仰化懷誠，馳慕聲教，皇風遐暨，荒服來款，是用加茲顯策，式甄義順。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu with patent of appointment made him King of Pada, saying: "Only you, looking up to transformation and holding sincerity in your heart, eagerly admiring the civilizing teaching—the imperial wind reaches afar, the wild domains come with sincere submission; therefore this splendid patent is added, to distinguish righteous obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen invested him as King of Pada with a patent reading: "You who look to our civilization with sincere hearts, eager for our teachings—imperial grace reaches even the remote frontier, and wild lands submit; we therefore bestow this splendid patent to honor your righteous loyalty.

sentences.zh: 爾其祗順憲典，永終休福，可不慎歟。」

translations.literal: You shall respectfully comply with the canonical statutes, forever securing blessed fortune—is this not to be heeded?"
translations.idiomatic: Obey the statutes and preserve your blessed realm to the end—can you do otherwise?"

sentences.zh: 二十六年、二十八年，復遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth and twenty-eighth years, [Panta] again sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth and twenty-eighth years (449, 451) envoys came again with tribute.

sentences.zh: 闍婆婆達國，[3]元嘉十二年，國王師黎婆達陁阿羅跋摩遣使奉表曰：[4]

translations.literal: The state of Shepoboda,[3] in the twelfth year of Yuanjia, King Shilipodatuohalobamo sent envoys with a memorial saying:[4]
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Shepoboda:[3] in the twelfth year of Yuanjia (435) King Shilipodatuohalobamo sent envoys with a memorial reading:[4]

sentences.zh: 宋國大主大吉天子足下：敬禮一切種智安隱，天人師降伏四魔，成等正覺，轉尊法輪，度脫眾生，教化已周，入于湼槃，舍利流布，起旡量塔，眾寶莊嚴，如須彌山，經法流布，如日照明，無量淨僧，猶如列宿。

translations.literal: To the Great Lord of Song, the Great Auspicious Son of Heaven, at your feet: I respectfully salute the All-Knowing One, peaceful and secure, Teacher of gods and men, who subdued the four demons, attained perfect enlightenment, turned the honored Dharma wheel, delivered all sentient beings, completed his teaching, entered nirvana, whose relics spread abroad, raising countless stupas adorned with myriad treasures like Mount Sumeru, whose scriptures and teachings spread like the sun's illumination, and whose countless pure monks are like constellations in array.
translations.idiomatic: To the Great Lord of Song, Most Auspicious Son of Heaven: I bow to the All-Knowing One at peace—the Teacher of gods and men who conquered the four demons, attained perfect enlightenment, turned the wheel of the Dharma, saved all beings, completed his teaching, and entered nirvana; whose relics spread across the land, raising countless jeweled stupas towering like Mount Sumeru; whose scriptures shine like the sun; and whose countless pure monks stand like stars in the heavens.

sentences.zh: 國界廣大，民人眾多，宮殿城郭，如忉利天宮。

translations.literal: Your realm is broad, your people numerous; palaces and walled cities are like the heavenly palace of Trayastrimsha.
translations.idiomatic: Your realm is vast, your people innumerable; your palaces and cities rival the halls of heaven.

sentences.zh: 名大宋揚州大國大吉天子，安處其中，紹繼先聖，王有四海，閻浮提內，莫不來服。

translations.literal: Named Great Song, the Great State of Yangzhou, the Great Auspicious Son of Heaven—you dwell therein, succeeding the former sages, ruling the four seas; within Jambudvipa, none fail to come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: You are known as the Most Auspicious Son of Heaven of Great Song, the great state of Yangzhou; you dwell secure within it, inheriting the sages of old and ruling the four seas—all within Jambudvipa bow to you.

sentences.zh: 悉以茲水，普飲一切，我雖在遠，亦霑靈潤，是以雖隔巨海，常遙臣屬，願照至誠，垂哀納受。

translations.literal: All with this water universally drink; though I am far away, I too am moistened by spiritual grace; therefore though separated by the great sea, I ever remain your distant subject; may you look upon my utmost sincerity and in mercy accept me.
translations.idiomatic: As all drink from these waters and receive their blessing, though I am far away I too share in your grace; though the great sea divides us, I remain your loyal subject in spirit. Look upon my sincere devotion and in mercy accept me.

sentences.zh: 若蒙聽許，當年遣信，若有所須，惟命是獻，伏願信受，不生異想。

translations.literal: If I may receive your gracious consent, I will send envoys the same year; if you have any need, I will offer whatever you command; I humbly wish you to believe and accept, without harboring other thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: If you grant my request, I will send envoys within the year; whatever you require, I shall supply on your command. I pray you will trust and accept me, without doubting my intent.

sentences.zh: 今遣使主佛大陁婆、副使葛抵奉宣微誠，稽首敬禮大吉天子足下，陁婆所啟，願見信受，諸有所請，唯願賜聽。

translations.literal: Now I send chief envoy Fotuopoduo and deputy envoy Gedi to convey my slight sincerity, kowtowing in respect to the Great Auspicious Son of Heaven at your feet; what Poduo reports, I wish to be believed and accepted; in all that I request, I only ask that you grant a hearing.
translations.idiomatic: I now send chief envoy Fotuopoduo and deputy envoy Gedi to convey my humble devotion, bowing before you, Most Auspicious Son of Heaven. I pray you will trust what Poduo reports, and grant every request I make.

sentences.zh: 今奉微物，以表微心。

translations.literal: Now I present slight goods to express my slight heart.
translations.idiomatic: I offer these modest gifts as tokens of my humble devotion.

sentences.zh: 師子國，元嘉五年，[5]國王剎利摩訶南奉表曰：

translations.literal: The state of Lion Country—in the fifth year of Yuanjia,[5] King Kshatriya Mahanam submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Sri Lanka: in the fifth year of Yuanjia (428),[5] King Kshatriya Mahanam submitted a memorial reading:

sentences.zh: 謹白大宋明主，雖山海殊隔，而音信時通。

translations.literal: I respectfully inform the enlightened lord of Great Song: though mountains and seas divide us extraordinarily, word and message reach each other in due season.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully address the enlightened ruler of Great Song: though mountains and seas stand between us, news still passes between our realms.

sentences.zh: 伏承皇帝道德高遠，覆載同於天地，明照齊乎日月，四海之外，無往不伏，方國諸王，莫不遣信奉獻，以表歸德之誠，或泛海三年，陸行千日，畏威懷德，無遠不至。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I have heard that the Emperor's virtue is lofty and far-reaching, his covering and bearing equal to heaven and earth, his brightness equal to sun and moon; beyond the four seas, wherever one goes none fail to submit; the kings of the various states all send envoys with faith and tribute to express their sincere submission to virtue; some cross the sea for three years or travel overland for a thousand days—awed by your might and cherishing your virtue, none so far as not to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Though I cannot see you in person, I know your virtue reaches as high and wide as heaven and earth, your wisdom shines like sun and moon; beyond the four seas none resists you. Princes of every realm send envoys bearing tribute in earnest submission. Some sail three years or march a thousand days—drawn by your power and goodness, none stays away.

sentences.zh: 我先王以來，唯以修德為正，不嚴而治，奉事三寶，道濟天下，欣人為善，慶若在己，欲與天子共弘正法，以度難化。

translations.literal: Since our former kings, we have taken cultivating virtue as our standard, governing without severity, serving the Three Treasures, using the Way to aid the world, rejoicing when others do good as if it were ourselves, wishing jointly with the Son of Heaven to spread the orthodox Law, to deliver those hard to transform.
translations.idiomatic: Since the time of my forefathers we have governed through virtue rather than force, honoring the Three Treasures, bringing the Way to the world, rejoicing in others' goodness as our own, and wishing together with Your Majesty to spread the true Dharma and save those hardest to convert.

sentences.zh: 故託四道人遣二白衣送牙臺像以為信誓，信還，願垂音告。

translations.literal: Therefore we entrusted four monks and sent two lay disciples bringing an ivory altar image as pledge of faith; when the envoys return, we wish you would extend your gracious word in reply.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore send four monks and two lay disciples bearing an ivory altar image as pledge of our faith; when our envoys return, we ask that you send word in reply.

sentences.zh: 至十二年，又復遣使奉獻。

translations.literal: By the twelfth year, [Sri Lanka] again sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (435) envoys came again with tribute.

sentences.zh: 天竺迦毗黎國，元嘉五年，國王月愛遣使奉表曰：

translations.literal: The state of Kapili in India—in the fifth year of Yuanjia, King Moon-Love sent envoys with a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Kapili in India: in the fifth year of Yuanjia (428) King Yue'ai sent envoys with a memorial reading:

sentences.zh: 伏聞彼國，據江傍海，山川周固，眾妙悉備，莊嚴清淨，猶如化城，宮殿莊嚴，街巷平坦，人民充滿，歡娛安樂。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I have heard of that state: nestled by rivers and beside the sea, mountains and rivers encircle it in solid strength, all excellences fully provided, solemn and pure as a conjured city; palaces majestic, streets and lanes level; people fill it, joyous and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: From afar I have heard of your realm: set between rivers and sea, ringed by mountains, endowed with every excellence, pure and splendid as a divine city—your palaces rise in majesty, your streets lie level, your people abound in joy and ease.

sentences.zh: 聖王出遊，四海隨從，聖明仁愛，不害眾生，萬邦歸仰，國富如海。

translations.literal: The sage king goes abroad on tour; the four seas follow; sage and bright, benevolent and loving, harming no sentient beings; the myriad states look up and submit; the state is rich as the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage king travels abroad, the four seas attend him. Wise, benevolent, harming no living thing, he draws every nation to homage; his kingdom's wealth is boundless as the sea.

sentences.zh: 國中眾生，奉順正法，大王仁聖，化之以道，慈施羣生，無所遺惜。

translations.literal: Within the state the myriad beings comply with the orthodox Law; the Great King is benevolent and sage, transforming them by the Way, bestowing mercy on all beings, sparing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects follow the true Law; the Great King, benevolent and sage, teaches them through the Way, showering mercy on all beings without stint.

sentences.zh: 帝修淨戒，軌道不及，無上法船，濟諸沈溺，羣僚百官，受樂無怨，諸天擁護，萬神侍衞，天魔降伏，莫不歸化。

translations.literal: The Emperor cultivates pure precepts—none can match his path and measure; the supreme Dharma vessel delivers all who are drowning; the assembled ministers and hundred officials receive joy without complaint; all heavens protect, myriad spirits attend; the heavenly demons are subdued; none fail to turn and submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor keeps pure precepts beyond compare; his supreme Dharma vessel rescues the drowning. Ministers and officials serve in contentment; the heavens protect him, myriad spirits attend him, demons are subdued—all submit to his rule.

sentences.zh: 王身端嚴，如日初出，仁澤普潤，猶如大雲，聖賢承業，如日月天，於彼真丹，最為殊勝。

translations.literal: The King's person is upright and solemn, like the sun first rising; benevolent favor spreads and moistens like a great cloud; sages and worthies inherit the enterprise like sun and moon in heaven; among those true lands, he is most extraordinary and superior.
translations.idiomatic: Your majesty stands upright as the rising sun; your benevolence spreads like rain from great clouds. Sages inherit your cause as sun and moon in the sky—among the true realms of the Dharma, yours is supreme.

sentences.zh: 臣之所住，名迦毗河，東際于海，其城四邊，悉紫紺石，首羅天護，令國安隱。

translations.literal: Where your subject dwells is called the Kapili River; eastward it reaches the sea; on all four sides its city is entirely of purple-blue stone; Shiluo Heaven protects it, keeping the state secure and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: My kingdom lies on the Kapili River, reaching eastward to the sea. Its walls on every side are built of purple stone; the god Shiluo protects us, keeping the land secure and at peace.

sentences.zh: 國王相承，未嘗斷絕，國中人民，率皆修善，諸國來集，共遵道法，諸寺舍子，皆七寶形像，眾妙供具，如先王法。

translations.literal: Kings have succeeded one another without interruption; the people of the state all for the most part cultivate goodness; various states come and gather, jointly following the Way and its teachings; in all temples and monasteries the images are of the seven treasures, with myriad fine offerings and implements, according to the law of former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Kings have ruled in unbroken succession; our people for the most part practice goodness. Foreign lands gather here to follow the Way. In every monastery the images are wrought of the seven treasures, with splendid offerings as in the time of former kings.

sentences.zh: 臣自修檢，不犯道禁，臣名月愛，棄世王種。

translations.literal: Your subject himself cultivates restraint and does not violate the prohibitions of the Way; your subject is named Moon-Love, having abandoned the royal lineage of the world.
translations.idiomatic: I myself keep the precepts and violate none of the Law. My name is Yue'ai; I have renounced my worldly royal lineage.

sentences.zh: 惟願大王聖體和善，羣臣百官，悉自安隱。

translations.literal: I only wish the Great King's sacred person harmony and goodness, and that all ministers and officials be secure and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I pray only that the Great King's sacred person enjoys health and harmony, and that all his ministers and officials live in peace.

sentences.zh: 今以此國羣臣吏民，山川珍寶，一切歸屬，五體歸誠大王足下。

translations.literal: Now I submit this state's assembled ministers, clerks, and people, its mountains, rivers, and treasures—all are given in allegiance; with all five limbs I return in sincerity to the Great King at your feet.
translations.idiomatic: I now submit this kingdom—all its officials, its people, its mountains, rivers, and treasures—to you in complete allegiance, bowing in full devotion at your feet.

sentences.zh: 山海遐隔，無由朝覲，宗仰之至，遣使下承。

translations.literal: Mountains and seas lie far apart; there is no means to come to court in audience; in the utmost of veneration, envoys are sent to receive your commands from below.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and seas lie between us, preventing my coming to court; in deepest reverence I send envoys to receive your commands.

sentences.zh: 使主父名天魔悉達，使主名尼陁達，此人由來良善忠信，是故今遣奉使表誠。

translations.literal: The chief envoy's father is named Heavenly Demon Siddhartha; the chief envoy is named Nitada; this person has always been good, loyal, and trustworthy; therefore he is now sent on mission to express sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy's father is named Tianmosida; the chief envoy is Nitada—a man always good, loyal, and trustworthy, whom I therefore send to testify to my sincerity.

sentences.zh: 大王若有所須，珍奇異物，悉當奉送，此之境土，便是王國，王之法令，治國善道，悉當承用。

translations.literal: If the Great King has any need, rare and strange things shall all be offered; this very territory shall be your kingdom; your laws and statutes, the good Way of governing the state—all shall be received and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever rare treasures you require, I shall send them. This land shall be your kingdom; your laws and wise governance I shall adopt in full.

sentences.zh: 願二國信使往來不絕，此反使還，願賜一使，具宣聖命，備勑所宜。

translations.literal: I wish envoys of the two states to come and go without cease; when these returning envoys come back, I wish you would send an envoy to declare fully the sacred command, fully preparing whatever orders are fitting.
translations.idiomatic: May envoys of our two realms travel back and forth without end. When these envoys return, I ask that you send one of your own to proclaim your sacred will in full.

sentences.zh: 款至之誠，望不空反，所白如是，願加哀愍。

translations.literal: Sincere devotion reaching to the utmost—I hope it will not return empty; what I have stated is thus; I wish you would extend compassion and pity.
translations.idiomatic: I pray this earnest devotion will not be sent away unanswered. This is my plea; I ask your compassion.

sentences.zh: 奉獻金剛指環、摩勒金環諸寶物、赤白鸚鵡各一頭。

translations.literal: Presenting a diamond finger-ring, a molila gold ring and various treasures, one red and one white parrot each.
translations.idiomatic: He offered a diamond finger ring, molila gold rings and other treasures, and one red and one white parrot.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始二年，又遣使貢獻，以其使主竺扶大、竺阿彌並為建威將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi under Emperor Taizong, [Kapili] again sent envoys with tribute, and its chief envoys Zhufuda and Zhuamituo were both made Generals Who Establish Might.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi (466), under Emperor Ming, envoys came again with tribute; chief envoys Zhufuda and Zhuamituo were both made Generals Who Establish Might.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十八年，蘇摩黎國王那隣那羅跋摩遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia, King Nalinnalobamo of Sumoli sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia (441) King Nalinnalobamo of Sumoli sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝建二年，斤陁利國王釋婆羅那隣陁遣長史竺留陁及多獻金銀寶器。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Shizu, King Shiboluanalintuo of Jintuoli sent his chief clerk Zhuliutuo and others presenting gold, silver, and precious vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian (455), under Emperor Xiaowu, King Shiboluanalintuo of Jintuoli sent his chief clerk Zhuliutuo and others with gold, silver, and precious vessels.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽元年，婆黎國遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor, the state of Poli sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhui (473), under Emperor Houfei, Poli sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸國，皆事佛道。

translations.literal: Generally, all these states served the Buddha-Way.
translations.idiomatic: All these kingdoms practiced Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 佛道自後漢明帝，法始東流，自此以來，其教稍廣，自帝王至于民庶，莫不歸心，經誥充積，訓義深遠，別為一家之學焉。

translations.literal: The Buddha-Way, from Emperor Ming of Later Han, when the Law first flowed east—since then its teaching has gradually broadened; from emperors and kings down to common people, none failed to turn their hearts; scriptural teachings piled in abundance, their instructive meaning deep and far-reaching—it became a separate school of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism entered China under Emperor Ming of the Later Han and gradually spread. From emperors to commoners, all turned to it. Scriptures accumulated in vast numbers, their teachings profound and far-reaching, until Buddhism stood as a distinct tradition.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，丹陽尹蕭摹之奏曰：「佛化被于中國，已歷四代，形像塔寺，所在千數，進可以繫心，[6]退足以招勸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia, Danyang Prefect Xiao Muzhi submitted a memorial saying: "The Buddha's teaching has covered China, already passing four generations; images, pagodas, and temples number in the thousands everywhere—advancing can bind the heart,[6] retreating is sufficient to summon and encourage.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia (435) Danyang prefect Xiao Muzhi memorialized: "Buddhism has flourished in China for four dynasties; images, pagodas, and temples number in the thousands—they can anchor the faithful[6] and draw others to devotion.

sentences.zh: 而自頃以來，情敬浮末，不以精誠為至，更以奢競為重。

translations.literal: But since recently, sentiment and reverence have floated to the surface; sincerity is not taken as the utmost, and instead lavish competition is prized.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately devotion has grown shallow; people no longer prize sincere faith, but compete in extravagance.

sentences.zh: 舊宇頹弛，曾莫之修，而各務造新，以相姱尚。

translations.literal: Old structures decay and collapse—no one repairs them; yet each strives to build new ones, to outshine one another in display.
translations.idiomatic: Old temples crumble unattended while everyone races to build new ones, each trying to outdo the rest.

sentences.zh: 甲第顯宅，於茲殆盡，材竹銅綵，糜損無極，無關神祇，有累人事。

translations.literal: Grand mansions and prominent houses are nearly exhausted for this; timber, bamboo, copper, and colored silks are wasted without limit—no relation to the spirits, but a burden on human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They squander timber, bamboo, copper, and silk without limit on temples that do nothing for the gods but weigh heavily on the people.

sentences.zh: 建中越制，宜加裁檢，不為之防，流遁未息。

translations.literal: Construction exceeds due measure—it should be cut back and inspected; if not guarded against, the drift and flight will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Such excess construction should be restrained; without checks the waste will never stop.

sentences.zh: [7]請自今以後，有欲鑄銅像者，悉詣臺自聞；

translations.literal: [7] I request that from now on, whoever wishes to cast bronze images must all go to the central administration and report in person;
translations.idiomatic: [7] I ask that from now on anyone wishing to cast bronze images must report to the central administration;

sentences.zh: 興造塔寺精舍，皆先詣在所二千石通辭，郡依事列言本州；

translations.literal: To raise pagodas, temples, and refined abodes, all must first go to the local Two-Thousand-Dan [official] to give notice; the commandery, according to the matter, shall report to the original province;
translations.idiomatic: Construction of pagodas, temples, and monasteries must first be announced to the local chief official, who shall report through the commandery to the province;

sentences.zh: 須許報，然後就功。

translations.literal: Permission must be granted in reply, and only then may work proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Work may begin only after approval is received.

sentences.zh: 其有輒造寺舍者，皆依不承用詔書律，銅宅林苑，悉沒入官。」

translations.literal: Whoever presumptuously builds temples and abodes shall all, according to the statute on not implementing edicts, have their bronze [images], residences, and wooded parks entirely confiscated for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who builds without permission shall be punished under the statute for defying imperial edicts; bronze images, properties, and orchards shall be confiscated."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又沙汰沙門，罷道者數百人。

translations.literal: Monks were also screened and purged; several hundred who left the Way were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Monks were also screened; several hundred were defrocked.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明二年，有曇標道人與羌人高闍謀反，上因是下詔曰：「佛法訛替，沙門混雜，未足扶濟鴻教，而專成逋藪。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming under Emperor Shizu, the monk Tanbiao plotted rebellion with the Qiang man Gao Ge; the Emperor therefore issued an edict: "The Buddha-Way has gone astray and declined; monks are mixed and confused—not sufficient to support and aid the great teaching, yet they have become a dedicated harbor of fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming (458), under Emperor Xiaowu, the monk Tanbiao conspired with the Qiang tribesman Gao Ge to rebel. The emperor then issued an edict: "Buddhism has fallen into decay; monks are a confused lot, failing to uphold the faith while harboring fugitives.

sentences.zh: 加姦心頻發，凶狀屢聞，敗亂風俗，人神交怨。

translations.literal: Moreover treacherous hearts frequently arise; violent deeds are repeatedly heard—corrupting customs; humans and spirits alike resent it.
translations.idiomatic: Treachery mounts, outrages multiply, morals are corrupted, and both men and gods are offended.

sentences.zh: 可付所在，精加沙汰，後有違犯，嚴加誅坐。」

translations.literal: Let local officials be entrusted [with this]: thoroughly screen and purge; hereafter whoever violates shall be strictly punished and penalized."
translations.idiomatic: Let local authorities conduct a thorough purge; future violators shall be severely punished."

sentences.zh: 於是設諸條禁，自非戒行精苦，並使還俗。

translations.literal: Thereupon various prohibitions were established; except for those whose precept-keeping and practice were refined and arduous, all were made to return to the laity.
translations.idiomatic: Many regulations followed; all monks except those of ascetic virtue were forced to return to lay life.

sentences.zh: 而諸寺尼出入宮掖，交關妃后，此制竟不能行。

translations.literal: Yet nuns of the various temples entered and left the inner palace, associating with consorts and empresses—this regulation in the end could not be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Yet temple nuns continued to enter the palace and consort with imperial women, and the policy could not be enforced.

sentences.zh: 先是晉世庾冰始創議，欲使沙門敬王者，後桓玄復述其義，並不果行。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Jin era Yu Bing first initiated the proposal, wishing to make monks reverence the king; later Huan Xuan again set forth the same principle—neither was carried out in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in the Jin, Yu Bing first proposed that monks bow to the emperor; Huan Xuan later revived the idea—but neither succeeded.

sentences.zh: 大明六年，世祖使有司奏曰：「臣聞邃宇崇居，非期宏峻，拳跪槃伏，非止敬恭，將以施張四維，締制八宇。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daming, Emperor Shizu had the relevant offices memorialize: "Your subject has heard that deep halls and lofty dwellings are not sought for vast grandeur; bowing fist to ground and prostration are not merely to show respectful reverence—they are meant to extend the four bonds and establish rule over the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daming (462), Emperor Xiaowu had officials memorialize: "Deep halls and lofty seats are not meant merely for grandeur; bowing and prostration serve not only as marks of respect—they uphold the four bonds and order the realm.

sentences.zh: 故雖儒法枝派，名墨條分，至於崇親嚴上，厥繇靡爽。

translations.literal: Therefore though Confucianism and the Law are branch lineages, Naming and Mohism are divided into articles—when it comes to honoring kin and reverencing superiors, the principle never errs.
translations.idiomatic: Though Confucianism, Legalism, Naming, and Mohism part into schools, all agree on honoring kin and reverencing superiors.

sentences.zh: 唯浮圖為教，逷自龍堆，反經提傳，訓遐事遠，練生瑩識，恒俗稱難，宗旨緬謝，微言淪隔，拘文蔽道，在末彌扇。

translations.literal: Only Buddhism as a teaching, reaching from Longdui, contradicts the classics and carries its transmission afar; its instructions are remote and its affairs distant; refining life and polishing understanding—the constant custom calls it difficult; its core doctrine fades and withdraws, subtle words sink and are cut off; clinging to the letter obscures the Way, and in recent times it spreads all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism alone, coming from beyond the western frontier, departs from the classics. Its teachings are remote, its doctrines difficult for ordinary people. Its core has grown obscure, its subtle words lost; literalism hides the Way, and lately it spreads only the more.

sentences.zh: 遂乃陵越典度，偃倨尊戚，失隨方之眇迹，迷製化之淵義。

translations.literal: Thereupon it oversteps canonical standards, stands erect and arrogant before honored kin, losing the subtle traces of adapting to circumstance, confused about the deep meaning of establishing transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Monks now overstep propriety, standing proud before noble kin, forgetting their place and the deeper purpose of civilizing rule.

sentences.zh: 夫佛法以謙儉自牧，忠虔為道，不輕比丘，遭人斯拜，[8]目連桑門，遇長則禮，寧有屈膝四輩，而簡禮二親，[9]稽顙耆臘，而直體萬乘者哉。

translations.literal: For the Buddha-Way teaches humility and self-restraint, loyal devotion as the Way—not lightly [honoring] a monk, yet when one encounters him one bows;[8] Mulian the monk, encountering elders then bows—is there one who kneels to the four assemblies yet abbreviates ritual toward the two kin,[9] who knocks forehead to aged monks yet stands upright before the ten-thousand-fold chariot?
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism teaches humility and loyal devotion—monks bow to elders, not the reverse.[8] Even Maudgalyayana bowed to his seniors.[9] How then can monks kneel to one another yet refuse to bow to parents, or prostrate before elders yet stand stiff before the emperor?

sentences.zh: 故咸康創議，元興載述，而事屈偏黨，道挫餘分。

translations.literal: Therefore the Xian Kang proposal was initiated, the Yuanxing account set forth—and yet the affair was thwarted by partisan bias, the Way discouraged in its remaining portion.
translations.idiomatic: Proposals at Xiankang and Yuanxing failed through partisan obstruction.

sentences.zh: 今鴻源遙洗，羣流仰鏡，九仙賮寶，百神聳職，而畿輦之內，舍弗臣之氓，陛席之間，延抗禮之客，懼非所以澄一風範，詳示景則者也。

translations.literal: Now the great source is washed from afar, the multitude of streams look up to the mirror; the nine immortals present treasures, the hundred spirits stand alert in duty—yet within the capital region dwell men who do not bow as subjects; between the throne and the mats extend guests who resist the ritual—this is feared not to be the means to clarify and unify the standard of conduct, to display clearly the pattern for all to see.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the dynasty shines bright and all look to the throne, yet within the capital live subjects who refuse to bow, and before the imperial seat stand guests who resist ritual—is this how to unify conduct and set a clear example?

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，以為沙門接見，比當盡虔禮敬之容，依其本俗，則朝徽有序，乘方兼遂矣。」

translations.literal: Your subjects jointly deliberated and consider that when monks are received in audience, they ought fully to show reverent and respectful bearing; according to their original custom—then court insignia will have order, and riding the direction, both aims will be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: We propose that when monks are received in audience they should show full reverence according to custom—thus court order will be preserved on every side."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，復舊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Former Deposed Emperor, [the old custom] was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Qianfei's reign the old practice was restored.

sentences.zh: 世祖寵姬殷貴妃薨，為之立寺，貴妃子子鸞封新安王，故以新安為寺號。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu's favored consort, Noble Consort Yin, died; for her a temple was established; the Noble Consort's son Ziluan was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an; therefore Xin'an was taken as the temple name.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu's beloved Consort Yin died, he built a temple in her honor. Her son Ziluan had been enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an, so the temple took that name.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝殺子鸞，乃毀廢新安寺，驅斥僧徒，尋又毀中興、天寶諸寺。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor killed Ziluan; thereupon he destroyed and abolished Xin'an Temple, drove out and expelled the monks—and soon after destroyed the Zhongxing, Tianbao, and other temples.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qianfei killed Ziluan, then demolished Xin'an Temple and expelled its monks; soon after he destroyed Zhongxing, Tianbao, and other temples as well.

sentences.zh: 太宗定亂，下令曰：「先帝建中興及新安諸寺，所以長世垂範，弘宣盛化。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong pacified the disorder and issued an order: "The Former Emperor built the Zhongxing and Xin'an temples and others—these were to extend the age and hand down a model, to spread broadly the flourishing teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, having quelled the rebellion, issued an order: "My predecessor built the Zhongxing and Xin'an temples to endure for generations and spread the flourishing teaching.

sentences.zh: 頃遇昏虐，法像殘毀，師徒奔迸，甚以矜懷。

translations.literal: Recently encountering deluded cruelty, Dharma images were mangled and destroyed, teachers and disciples fled and scattered—greatly to be pitied and held in concern.
translations.idiomatic: Under recent tyranny their images were destroyed and their monks scattered—a cause for deep sorrow.

sentences.zh: 妙訓淵謨，有扶名教。

translations.literal: Profound instructions and deep counsels have power to support the name and teaching [of Confucianism].
translations.idiomatic: Their profound teachings can still support the moral order.

sentences.zh: 可招集舊僧，普各還本，並使材官，隨宜修復。」

translations.literal: Let the former monks be gathered and recalled, all each returning to their origins, and also send military craftsmen to repair as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Recall the former monks to their temples and send craftsmen to restore them as needed."

sentences.zh: 宋世名僧有道生。

translations.literal: Among famous monks of the Song era was Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: A renowned monk of the Liu Song was Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 道生，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Daosheng was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng was from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 父為廣戚令。

translations.literal: His father was magistrate of Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: His father served as magistrate of Guangqi.

sentences.zh: 生出家為沙門法大弟子。

translations.literal: Sheng left home and became a disciple of the monk Fada.
translations.idiomatic: He left home to become a disciple of the monk Fada.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰悟，年十五，便能講經。

translations.literal: From childhood he was bright and comprehending; at age fifteen he could already expound sutras.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was brilliant; by fifteen he could expound the sutras.

sentences.zh: 及長有異解，立頓悟義，時人推服之。

translations.literal: When grown he had unusual understanding; he established the doctrine of sudden enlightenment—and people of the time admired and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he developed distinctive views and formulated the doctrine of sudden enlightenment, which won wide admiration.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十一年，卒於廬山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia, he died on Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He died on Mount Lu in the eleventh year of Yuanjia (434).

sentences.zh: 沙門慧琳為之誄。

translations.literal: The monk Huilin wrote a eulogy for him.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huilin composed his elegy.

sentences.zh: 慧琳者，秦郡秦縣人，姓劉氏。

translations.literal: Huilin was a man of Qin County, Qin Commandery, surname Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Huilin was from Qin County in Qin Commandery, of the Liu clan.

sentences.zh: 少出家，住冶城寺，有才章，兼外內之學，為廬陵王義真所知。

translations.literal: From youth he left home and lived at Ye City Temple; he had literary talent and combined inner and outer learning—and was appreciated by Prince of Luling Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: He entered monastic life young at Yecheng Temple, excelled in both Buddhist and secular learning, and won the favor of Prince Yizhen of Luling.

sentences.zh: 嘗著均善論，其詞曰：

translations.literal: He once composed the Treatise on Equilibrium and Goodness; its words say:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Treatise on Equilibrium and Goodness, which begins:

sentences.zh: 有白學先生，以為中國聖人，經綸百世，其德弘矣，智周萬變，天人之理盡矣，道無隱旨，教罔遺筌，聰叡迪哲，何負於殊論哉。

translations.literal: There was a Master of White Learning who considered that China's sages governed and organized the hundred generations—their virtue was vast, their wisdom encompassed the myriad things, the principles of heaven and man were complete; the Way had no hidden purport, teaching left no net untended; bright and wise, leading to enlightenment—how could they fall short before alien doctrines?
translations.idiomatic: A master of White Learning held that China's sages had governed for generations with vast virtue and all-encompassing wisdom, leaving no principle of heaven or man unexplored—their Way hid nothing, their teaching omitted nothing. How could they be inferior to foreign creeds?

sentences.zh: 有黑學道士陋之，謂不照幽冥之途，弗及來生之化，雖尚虛心，未能虛事，不逮西域之深也。
