translations.literal: A Daoist priest of Black Learning looked down on this, saying [White Learning] did not illuminate the path through the dark underworld, did not reach the transformation of the next life; though it prized empty mind, it could not empty affairs—not equal to the Western Region's depth.
translations.idiomatic: A priest of Black Learning scorned this, saying it illumined neither the underworld nor the afterlife—that though it prized emptiness of mind, it could not empty worldly affairs, and fell short of the depth of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 於是白學訪其所以不逮云爾。

translations.literal: Thereupon White Learning inquired into the reasons for this falling short—the words were thus.
translations.idiomatic: White Learning then asked precisely where it fell short.

sentences.zh: 白曰：「釋氏所論之空，與老氏所言之空，無同異乎？」

translations.literal: White said: "Is the emptiness discussed by the Shakya clan the same as or different from the emptiness spoken of by Master Lao?"
translations.idiomatic: White asked: "Is the emptiness taught by the Buddha the same as or different from Lao Zi's emptiness?"

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「異。

translations.literal: Black said: "Different.
translations.idiomatic: Black answered: "Different.

sentences.zh: 釋氏即物為空，空物為一。

translations.literal: The Shakya clan takes things as emptiness; emptiness and things are one.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha treats things as empty and merges emptiness with things into one.

sentences.zh: 老氏有無兩行，空有為異。

translations.literal: Master Lao has the two paths of being and non-being; emptiness and being are different.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Zi holds both being and non-being; for him emptiness and being differ.

sentences.zh: 安得同乎。」

translations.literal: How could they be the same?"
translations.idiomatic: How can they be the same?

sentences.zh: 白曰：「釋氏空物，物信空邪？」

translations.literal: White said: "The Shakya clan empties things—do things truly become empty?"
translations.idiomatic: White asked: "If the Buddha empties things, are things truly empty?"

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「然。

translations.literal: Black said: "Yes.
translations.idiomatic: Black replied: "Yes.

sentences.zh: 空又空，不翅於空矣。」

translations.literal: Empty again empty—no different from empty."
translations.idiomatic: Emptiness upon emptiness—nothing remains but emptiness itself.

sentences.zh: 白曰：「三儀靈長於宇宙，萬品盈生於天地，孰是空哉？」

translations.literal: White said: "The three powers spiritually endure throughout the cosmos; the myriad kinds fill and live from heaven and earth—which of these is empty?"
translations.idiomatic: White asked: "Heaven, earth, and man endure throughout the cosmos; all creatures teem upon the land—which of these is empty?

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「空其自性之有，不害因假之體也。

translations.literal: Black said: "Empty their self-nature's having—the constructed provisional body is not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Black replied: "It empties only their inherent existence, without denying their conventional forms.

sentences.zh: 今構羣材以成大廈，罔專寢之實，積一豪以致合抱，無檀木之體，有生莫俄頃之留，泰山蔑累息之固，興滅無常，因緣無主，所空在於性理，所難據於事用，吾以為悞矣。」

translations.literal: Now one constructs many materials to form a great hall—there is no reality of a sole sleeping chamber; one accumulates a single fine hair to reach a tree-trunk's girth—there is no sandalwood body; the living do not remain for a moment; Mount Tai scorns the solidity of accumulated breath; rise and fall are without constancy; dependent origination has no master; what is emptied lies in nature and principle; what is hard to establish lies in practical use—I consider that [objection] mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: Timbers are joined to raise a hall, yet no single "sleeping chamber" exists apart from the whole; hairs are piled until they would gird a tree, yet no sandalwood trunk is there. Nothing that lives endures a breath; even Mount Tai is not eternally firm. All things rise and fall without fixity; causes and conditions have no sovereign lord. Emptiness applies to intrinsic nature, not to practical use—and I hold your objection to be in error.

sentences.zh: 白曰：「所言實相，空者其如是乎？」

translations.literal: White said: "The real mark of which you speak—is emptiness truly thus?"
translations.idiomatic: White asked: "The ultimate reality you describe—is emptiness really like this?

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「然。」

translations.literal: Black said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: Black answered: "It is.

sentences.zh: 白曰：「浮變之理，交於目前，視聽者之所同了邪？

translations.literal: White said: "The principle of floating change intersects before the eyes—is it what those who see and hear alike comprehend?
translations.idiomatic: White pressed on: "The flux of change is plain before our eyes—is this not what every eye sees and every ear hears alike?

sentences.zh: 解之以登道場，重之以輕異學，誠未見其淵深。」

translations.literal: To explain it by ascending the Dharma platform, and to weigh it down with slighting alien learning—truly I have not seen its abyssal depth."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you would climb the Dharma seat to expound it, and dismiss rival teachings as shallow—I see no profundity in that.

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「斯理若近，求之實遠。

translations.literal: Black said: "This principle, if it seems near, in seeking it is truly far.
translations.idiomatic: Black replied: "This truth seems close at hand, yet pursued in earnest it recedes beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 夫情之所重者虛，事之可重者實。

translations.literal: What the emotions value heavily is the empty; what affairs can value heavily is the real.
translations.idiomatic: The heart must cherish what is empty; affairs must be grounded in what is real.

sentences.zh: 今虛其真實，離其浮偽，愛欲之惑，不得不去。

translations.literal: Now empty the true and real, leave behind the floating and false—the delusion of love and desire cannot but be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Empty what is truly real, cast off what is merely false, and the snares of craving cannot remain.

sentences.zh: 愛去而道場不登者，吾不知所以相曉也。」

translations.literal: If love is removed yet one does not ascend the Dharma platform—I do not know by what means we could make each other understand."
translations.idiomatic: If craving is gone and one still will not take the Dharma seat, I see no way we could ever understand each other.

sentences.zh: 白曰：「今析豪空樹，無□垂蔭之茂，離材虛室，不損輪奐之美，明無常增其愒蔭之情，陳若偏篤其競辰之慮。

translations.literal: White said: "Now split a fine hair and empty the tree—without □ shade-lending luxuriance; separate materials and empty the chamber—the splendor of its beams and eaves is not diminished; making clear impermanence increases the feeling of resting in shade; setting forth such partial earnestness heightens the anxiety of competing for time.
translations.idiomatic: White said: "Split a hair and the tree is 'empty'—yet no □ branching shade remains; dismantle the timbers and the room is 'empty'—yet its carved beams lose none of their beauty. Proclaim impermanence and you only deepen the longing for shade; preach such one-sided zeal and you only sharpen the dread of the passing day.

sentences.zh: 貝錦以繁采發輝，和羹以鹽梅致旨，齊矦追爽鳩之樂，燕王無延年之術，恐和合之辯，危脆之教，正足戀其嗜好之欲，無以傾其愛競之惑也。」

translations.literal: Shell brocade shines through many-colored brilliance; harmonized broth achieves its savor through salt and plum; the Marquis of Qi pursued the music of the Shuangjiu bird; the King of Yan had no art of prolonging life—I fear that arguments of harmony and teaching of fragility just suffice to fix their cravings and desires, and cannot overturn the delusion of love and rivalry."
translations.idiomatic: Brocade gleams through many hues; stew finds its flavor in salt and plum. The Marquis of Qi chased the Shuangjiu bird's song; the King of Yan knew no art of long life. I fear your talk of harmony and your doctrine of fragility only feed the appetites they claim to cure, and cannot uproot the passions of love and rivalry.

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「斯固理絕於諸華，墳素莫之及也。」

translations.literal: Black said: "This principle is indeed cut off from the various [teachings of] Huaxia—the classics and histories cannot reach it."
translations.idiomatic: Black answered: "This truth lies beyond anything Huaxia has known—the classics and histories cannot touch it.

sentences.zh: 白曰：「山高累卑之辭，川樹積小之詠，舟壑火傳之談，堅白唐肆之論，蓋盈於中國矣，非理之奧，故不舉以為教本耳。

translations.literal: White said: "The words that mountains are high through accumulated lowliness, the odes that streams and trees accumulate from the small, the talk of boats in gullies and fire passed on, the discourse of hard-white and Tang-market— these fill China; they are not the profundity of principle, and so are not taken as the root of teaching.
translations.idiomatic: White replied: "China already overflows with such sayings—that mountains grow high from humble stones, that rivers and trees grow great from small beginnings, that boats vanish into ravines and fire passes from torch to torch, that hard-white and Tang-market sophistries abound. They are not the deepest truth, and so are not made the foundation of teaching.

sentences.zh: 子固以遺情遺累，虛心為道，而據事剖析者，更由指掌之間乎。」

translations.literal: You indeed, by abandoning emotion and abandoning burden, take empty mind as the Way—yet when you analyze according to affairs, is it not again within the space between finger and palm?"
translations.idiomatic: You claim to cast off passion and burden and make an empty heart your Way—yet when you dissect things case by case, is that not still within fingertip's reach?

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「周、孔為教，正及一世，不見來生無窮之緣，積善不過子孫之慶，累惡不過餘殃之罰，報効止於榮祿，誅責極於窮賤，視聽之外，冥然不知，良可悲矣。

translations.literal: Black said: "Zhou and Confucius as teaching reach only one lifetime—they do not see the boundless conditions of the next life; accumulated goodness extends no further than descendants' blessing; accumulated evil extends no further than residual calamity's punishment; recompense stops at glory and salary; blame and punishment end at poverty and baseness; beyond sight and hearing, darkly unknowing—truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Black said: "The teaching of Zhou and Confucius extends only to this one life. It knows nothing of the boundless karma of lives to come. Goodness brings blessing no further than one's descendants; evil brings punishment no further than later generations. Reward stops at rank and emolument; punishment ends in poverty and disgrace. Beyond what eye and ear can reach, all is darkness—how lamentable.

sentences.zh: 釋迦關無窮之業，拔重關之險，陶方寸之慮，宇宙不足盈其明，設一慈之救，羣生不足勝其化，敍地獄則民懼其罪，敷天堂則物歡其福，指泥洹以長歸，乘法身以遐覽，神變無不周，靈澤靡不覃，先覺翻翔於上世，後悟騰翥而不紹，坎井之局，何以識大方之家乎。」

translations.literal: Shakyamuni closes off boundless karma, pulls out the peril of heavy barriers, molds thoughts of a square inch—the cosmos is insufficient to fill his brightness; he sets up one compassionate salvation—the multitude of beings is insufficient to exhaust his transformation; narrating hell, then the people fear their sins; spreading heaven, then things rejoice in their blessings; pointing to nirvana as long homecoming, riding the Dharma-body to gaze far—divine transformation nowhere not complete, spiritual grace nowhere not extending; early awakened ones soar in former ages, later enlightened ones rise and fly without end—a pit-and-well's confines—how could one know the house of the great direction?"
translations.idiomatic: Shakyamuni seals off the karma of countless lives and breaks through the heaviest barriers. He refines the mind within a square inch, yet his light outfills the cosmos. With one compassionate deliverance he transforms all beings beyond counting. Describe hell and people fear their sins; preach heaven and all rejoice in its blessings. Point to nirvana as the long homecoming; mount the Dharma-body and survey the far reaches. His divine transformations leave nothing untouched; his grace extends everywhere. Sages of old soared in ages past; the awakened of later times rise without end. How can one trapped in a well know the dwelling of the truly great?

sentences.zh: 白曰：「固能大其言矣，今効神光無徑寸之明，驗靈變罔纖介之異，勤誠者不覩善救之貌，篤學者弗剋陵虛之實，徒稱無量之壽，孰見期頤之叟，咨嗟金剛之固，安覿不朽之質。

translations.literal: White said: "Indeed you can magnify your words; now testing divine light, there is no inch-breadth of brightness; verifying spiritual transformation, there is no fine-part's difference; the diligent and sincere do not behold the countenance of good salvation; the earnest learners cannot overcome the reality of ascending emptiness; vainly claiming measureless life—who has seen an old man of a hundred years? Sighing over the vajra's firmness—where is the imperishable substance seen?
translations.idiomatic: White said: "You can certainly enlarge your rhetoric. Yet when tested, divine light shows not even an inch of radiance; miraculous change reveals not the slightest trace. The devout see no face of salvation; the earnest student gains no proof of transcending the void. You speak of measureless life—who has met a man of a hundred years? You praise the diamond's hardness—where is this imperishable substance to be seen?

sentences.zh: 苟於事不符，宜尋立言之指，遺其所寄之說也。

translations.literal: If it does not accord with affairs, one ought to seek the aim of the words as set forth, and leave aside the doctrine to which they are entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: When words fail the test of affairs, one should seek what the speaker truly meant and set aside the doctrine he merely used to say it.

sentences.zh: 且要天堂以就善，曷若服義而蹈道，懼地獄以敕身，孰與從理以端心。

translations.literal: Moreover, to require heaven in order to do good—how does that compare with submitting to righteousness and treading the Way? To fear hell in order to restrain the body—who compares with following principle to rectify the heart?
translations.idiomatic: To demand heaven as the price of virtue—is that better than embracing righteousness and walking the Way? To fear hell as the curb on conduct—is that better than following reason and setting the heart aright?

sentences.zh: 禮拜以求免罪，不由祗肅之意，施一以徼百倍，弗乘無吝之情。

translations.literal: Prostrating in worship to seek escape from sin—not proceeding from reverent solemnity of intent; giving one to demand a hundredfold—not riding the feeling of giving without stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: One bows in worship to buy release from sin, not from reverent awe; one gives a single coin to claim a hundredfold return, not from unstinting generosity.

sentences.zh: 美泥洹之樂，生耽逸之慮，贊法身之妙，肇好奇之心，近欲未弭，遠利又興，雖言菩薩無欲，羣生固以有欲矣。

translations.literal: Praising nirvana's bliss gives rise to indulgent ease in thought; praising the Dharma-body's marvel initiates a heart of curious novelty; near desires not yet extinguished, far profit again arises—though one says bodhisattvas are without desire, the multitude of beings are inherently with desire.
translations.idiomatic: Praise nirvana's bliss and you breed longing for ease; praise the marvel of the Dharma-body and you stir a taste for novelty. Near cravings are not stilled before far rewards are dangled. Though you say bodhisattvas are without desire, ordinary beings remain creatures of desire.

sentences.zh: 甫救交敝之氓，永開利競之俗，澄神反道，其可得乎。」

translations.literal: Just saving the mutually exhausted common folk—forever opening a custom of profit and rivalry; clarifying spirit and returning to the Way—can this be obtained?"
translations.idiomatic: You would rescue people worn down by strife, yet open forever a culture of gain and rivalry. Can spirit be clarified and the Way recovered by such means?

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Black said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Black replied: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 若不示以來生之欲，何以權其當生之滯。

translations.literal: If one does not show them the desires of the next life, by what means can one weigh against the stagnation of this present life?
translations.idiomatic: Unless you hold out the desires of the next life, how can you counter the inertia of this one?

sentences.zh: 物情不能頓至，故積漸以誘之。

translations.literal: The disposition of things cannot arrive all at once; therefore one accumulates gradual steps to entice them.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature cannot leap to the goal at once; one must lure it forward step by step.

sentences.zh: 奪此俄頃，要彼無窮，若弗勤春稼，秋穡何期。

translations.literal: Take away this brief moment, require that boundlessness—if one does not labor at spring planting, when can autumn harvest be expected?
translations.idiomatic: Relinquish this fleeting moment for that boundless reward—without sowing in spring, what harvest can autumn bring?

sentences.zh: 端坐井底，而息意庶慮者，長淪於九泉之下矣。」

translations.literal: Sitting upright at the bottom of a well, yet ceasing intent and many thoughts—one will long sink beneath the nine springs."
translations.idiomatic: Sit upright in the bottom of a well and still your thoughts—you will sink forever beneath the nine springs.

sentences.zh: 白曰：「異哉！

translations.literal: White said: "Strange!
translations.idiomatic: White exclaimed: "How strange!

sentences.zh: 何所務之乖也。

translations.literal: How perverse is the aim pursued!
translations.idiomatic: How perverse is the course you pursue!

sentences.zh: 道在無欲，而以有欲要之，北行求郢，西征索越，方長迷於幽都，永謬滯於昧谷。

translations.literal: The Way lies in no desire, yet you use desire to require it—going north to seek Ying, marching west to seek Yue; just growing lost in Youdu, forever wrongly stuck at Migu.
translations.idiomatic: The Way lies in freedom from desire, yet you would reach it through desire—like going north to find Ying or marching west to seek Yue, growing ever more lost in the dark north while forever stranded at the western sunset.

sentences.zh: 遼遼閩、楚，其可見乎。

translations.literal: Far, far are Min and Chu—can they be seen?
translations.idiomatic: Min and Chu lie immeasurably far—can they ever be reached?

sentences.zh: 所謂積漸者，日損之謂也。

translations.literal: What is called gradual accumulation is what is called daily decrease.
translations.idiomatic: What you call gradual progress, I call daily diminishment.

sentences.zh: 當先遺其所輕，然後忘其所重，使利欲日去，淳白自生耳。

translations.literal: One ought first to abandon what is light, then forget what is heavy—making profit and desire daily depart, pure whiteness naturally arising.
translations.idiomatic: First let go of what is slight, then forget what weighs heavily, until profit and desire fall away day by day and purity arises of itself.

sentences.zh: 豈得以少要多，以粗易妙，俯仰之間，非利不動，利之所蕩，其有極哉。

translations.literal: How can one use the small to demand the much, use the coarse to exchange for the subtle—in the space of a bow, nothing moves unless for profit; what profit stirs—does it have a limit?
translations.idiomatic: How can the lesser demand the greater, the coarse trade for the subtle? In every motion, nothing stirs except for gain—and where gain leads, is there any end?

sentences.zh: 乃丹青眩媚綵之目，土木夸好壯之心，興糜費之道，單九服之財，樹無用之事，割羣生之急，致營造之計，成私樹之權，務勸化之業，結師黨之勢，苦節以要厲精之譽，護法以展陵競之情，悲矣。

translations.literal: Then vermilion and green dazzle eyes with charming colors; earth and wood boast hearts with love of grandeur—raising a path of wasteful expenditure, exhausting the wealth of the nine domains; planting useless affairs, cutting off the urgent needs of the multitude of beings; bringing about plans of construction, completing the power of private patronage; striving at the work of exhortation and conversion, forming the momentum of master-and-disciple factions; bitter austerity to demand the reputation of stern refinement; protecting the Dharma to display overbearing rivalry of feeling—lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Paint and lacquer dazzle the eye; timber and stone feed a lust for grandeur. Extravagance drains the wealth of the realm; useless projects displace the people's urgent needs. Building schemes become private patronage; preaching becomes the forging of sectarian power. Harsh asceticism wins a name for fierce devotion; defending the Dharma becomes a theater for domineering rivalry. How lamentable.

sentences.zh: 夫道其安寄乎。

translations.literal: The Way—where indeed can it be entrusted?
translations.idiomatic: Where, then, can the Way find a home?

sentences.zh: 是以周、孔敦俗，弗關視聽之外，老、莊陶風，謹守性分而已。」

translations.literal: Therefore Zhou and Confucius thickly cultivated custom—they did not concern what lies beyond sight and hearing; Lao and Zhuang molded the wind—they merely carefully kept to their allotted nature."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Confucius cultivated custom and did not meddle with what lies beyond sight and hearing. Lao Zi and Zhuang Zi shaped the age by urging each person to keep to his natural place—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「三遊本於仁義，盜跖資於五善，聖跡之敝，豈有內外。

translations.literal: Black said: "The three wanderers root in benevolence and righteousness; Robber Zhi draws support from the five goods—the traces of sages' decline—how could there be inner and outer?
translations.idiomatic: Black said: "The three wanderers drew on benevolence and righteousness; Robber Zhi drew on the five virtues. When the sages' legacy decays, is the rot confined to one camp alone?

sentences.zh: 且黃、老之家，符章之偽，水祝之誣，不可勝論。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the houses of Huang and Lao, talisman-chapters' falsity, water-prayer's deception—cannot be fully enumerated in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: And among the followers of Huang-Lao, the fraud of talismanic writs and the deceit of water-rites are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 子安於彼，駭於此，玩於濁水，違於清淵耳。」

translations.literal: You are at ease with that, alarmed at this; playing in muddy water, turning away from the clear deep."
translations.idiomatic: You are at ease with that and alarmed by this—playing in muddy water while turning from the clear deep.

sentences.zh: 白曰：「有跡不能不敝，有術不能無偽，此乃聖人所以桎梏也。

translations.literal: White said: "Where there are traces, decline cannot but come; where there are methods, falsity cannot be absent—this is why sages impose shackles.
translations.idiomatic: White replied: "Where there are traces, decay follows; where there are methods, fraud appears. That is why the sages set limits.

sentences.zh: 今所惜在作法於貪，遂以成俗，不正其敝，反以為高耳。

translations.literal: What is regretted now is making law in greed, thereby forming custom—not correcting its decline, but instead taking it as lofty.
translations.idiomatic: What I lament is that greed has been made into practice and then into custom—that its corruption is not corrected but celebrated as virtue.

sentences.zh: 至若淫妄之徒，世自近鄙，源流蔑然，固不足論。」

translations.literal: As for licentious and reckless sorts, the age itself draws near and despises them; source and stream are obliterated—they indeed are not worth discussing."
translations.idiomatic: As for the licentious and deluded, the age itself holds them in contempt; their line is already spent and not worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「釋氏之教，專救夷俗，便無取於諸華邪？」

translations.literal: Black said: "The teaching of the Shakya clan specially saves barbarian custom—then it has nothing to take from the various [lands of] Huaxia?"
translations.idiomatic: Black asked: "If the Buddha's teaching was meant only to redeem barbarian ways, does it have nothing to offer Huaxia?

sentences.zh: 白曰：「曷為其然。

translations.literal: White said: "Why should it be so?
translations.idiomatic: White answered: "Why should that be so?

sentences.zh: 為則開端，宜懷屬緒，愛物去殺，尚施周人，息心遺榮華之願，大士布兼濟之念，仁義玄一者，何以尚之。

translations.literal: If it acts, then it opens the beginning—one ought to cherish attachment to the thread; loving things and removing killing, still bestowing upon Zhou people; resting the heart and abandoning the wish for glory and splendor; great beings spread the thought of universal aid—benevolence, righteousness, and the darkly one—how could one still exalt it?
translations.idiomatic: From the outset it opened a path worth following: cherish all life and renounce killing; give freely even to the people of Zhou; still the heart and leave aside the hunger for glory; great beings spread the resolve to save all. When benevolence, righteousness, and the deepest unity are already present, what higher thing remains to exalt?

sentences.zh: 惜乎幽旨不亮，末流為累耳。」

translations.literal: Pity that the hidden purport is not bright; the later current becomes burden—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: It is only a pity that its subtle intent has grown dim and its later followers have become a burden.

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「子之論善殆同矣，便事盡於生乎？」

translations.literal: Black said: "Your discourse on goodness is nearly the same—then are affairs exhausted in this life?"
translations.idiomatic: Black said: "Your view of goodness is nearly the same as mine—yet would you limit all affairs to this life alone?

sentences.zh: 白曰：「幽冥之理，固不極於人事矣。

translations.literal: White said: "The principle of the dark underworld—indeed it is not exhausted in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: White replied: "The realm beyond life is not wholly knowable through human affairs.

sentences.zh: 周、孔疑而不辨，釋迦辨而不實，將宜廢其顯晦之跡，存其所要之旨。

translations.literal: Zhou and Confucius doubted but did not discriminate; Shakyamuni discriminated but not truly—one ought to abandon their bright-and-dark traces and preserve the purport they require.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Confucius doubted but did not presume to decide; Shakyamuni decided but could not prove his case. We should set aside their conflicting outward claims and keep what each truly intended.

sentences.zh: 請嘗言之。

translations.literal: Allow me to try to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Let me explain.

sentences.zh: 夫道之以仁義者，服理以從化，帥之以勸戒者，循利而遷善。

translations.literal: Those who lead by benevolence and righteousness—submit to principle and follow transformation; those who command by exhortation and admonition—follow profit and shift toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Those led by benevolence and righteousness submit to reason and are transformed; those guided by reward and warning follow advantage and turn toward good.

sentences.zh: 故甘辭興於有欲，而滅於悟理，淡說行於天解，而息於貪偽。

translations.literal: Therefore sweet words arise where there is desire, and are extinguished in comprehending principle; plain discourse proceeds where there is heaven's understanding, and rests where greed and falsity end.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet words arise where desire remains and fade once principle is understood; plain teaching suits those heaven has awakened and stills where greed and falsehood cease.

sentences.zh: 是以示來生者，蔽虧於道、釋不得已，杜幽闇者，冥符於姬、孔閉其兌。

translations.literal: Therefore showing the next life—Dao and Shakya, having no choice, obscure and diminish; shutting off the dark and hidden—darkly accord with Ji and Confucius closing their openings.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the talk of future lives: Daoists and Buddhists, having no alternative, veil the truth; the silence about the dark beyond: the Zhou and Confucius, in their own way, closed the gate.

sentences.zh: 由斯論之，言之者未必遠，知之者未必得，不知者未必失，但知六度與五教並行，信順與慈悲齊立耳。

translations.literal: From this to discuss it—those who speak are not necessarily far; those who know are not necessarily attaining; those who do not know are not necessarily losing—only know that the six paramitas and the five teachings proceed together, faith and obedience stand level with compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Seen this way, those who speak are not necessarily far from truth; those who know are not necessarily enlightened; those who do not know are not necessarily lost. Know only that the six paramitas may walk beside the five virtues, and that faith and obedience may stand together with compassion.

sentences.zh: 殊塗而同歸者，不得守其發輪之轍也。」

translations.literal: Those of different paths yet the same return—one cannot keep to the rut of the wheel's first track."
translations.idiomatic: Different roads may lead to the same end—but one need not cling to the first rut the wheel cut."

sentences.zh: 論行於世。

translations.literal: The treatise circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The treatise circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 舊僧謂其貶黜釋氏，欲加擯斥。

translations.literal: Old monks considered that it demeaned and dismissed the Shakya clan, and wished to add rejection and expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Older monks took it as an attack on Buddhism and sought to have him ostracized.

sentences.zh: 太祖見論賞之，元嘉中，遂參權要，朝廷大事，皆與議焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu saw the treatise and rewarded it; during Yuanjia, he then participated in power and importance—great affairs of court were all deliberated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen read the treatise and praised it. During the Yuanjia era Huilin entered the circle of power and was consulted on major state matters.

sentences.zh: 賓客輻湊，門車常有數十兩，四方贈賂相係，勢傾一時。

translations.literal: Guests gathered like wheel spokes; at the gate chariots often numbered several tens; gifts and bribes from the four directions linked in succession—influence tilted the age.
translations.idiomatic: Visitors flocked to his door and dozens of carriages often lined the street; gifts poured in from every quarter, and for a time his influence eclipsed all others.

sentences.zh: 注孝經及莊子逍遙篇、文論，傳於世。

translations.literal: He annotated the Classic of Filial Piety, Zhuang Zi's "Free and Easy Wandering" chapter, and Literary Discourses—these circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety, the "Free and Easy Wandering" chapter of the Zhuang Zi, and the Literary Discourses also circulated.

sentences.zh: 又有慧嚴、慧議道人，並住東安寺，學行精整，為道俗所推。

translations.literal: There were also the Daoist priests Huiyan and Huiyi, both dwelling at Dong'an Temple—learning and conduct refined and orderly, pushed forward by monks and laity alike.
translations.idiomatic: The monks Huiyan and Huiyi also lived at Dong'an Temple, men of refined learning and conduct esteemed by clergy and laity alike.

sentences.zh: 時鬭場寺多禪僧，京師為之語曰：「鬭場禪師窟，東安談義林。」

translations.literal: At the time Dou Arena Temple had many Chan monks; the capital made a saying about it: "Dou Arena—a den of Chan masters; Dong'an—a grove of doctrinal discourse."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Dou Arena Temple was known for its Chan monks, and a saying circulated in the capital: "Dou Arena—a cave of meditation masters; Dong'an—a forest of doctrinal debate."

sentences.zh: 世祖大明四年，於中興寺設齋。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming under Emperor Shizu, a vegetarian feast was set at Zhongxing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming (460), Emperor Xiaowu held a vegetarian feast at Zhongxing Temple.

sentences.zh: 有一異僧，眾莫之識，問其名，答言名明慧，從天安寺來，忽然不見。

translations.literal: There was one strange monk whom the assembly did not recognize; asked his name, he answered that his name was Minghui, that he came from Tian'an Temple—and suddenly he was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: A strange monk appeared whom no one recognized. Asked his name, he said he was Minghui and had come from Tian'an Temple—then vanished without warning.

sentences.zh: 天下無此寺名，乃改中興曰天安寺。

translations.literal: Under heaven there was no temple of this name; thereupon Zhongxing was changed to Tian'an Temple.
translations.idiomatic: No temple by that name existed anywhere in the realm, so Zhongxing Temple was renamed Tian'an Temple.

sentences.zh: 大明中，外國沙門摩訶衍苦節有精理，於京都多出新經，勝鬘經尤見重內學。

translations.literal: During Daming, the foreign monk Mahayana, through bitter austerity possessing refined principle, in the capital often produced new sutras—the Shravakabhumi Sutra especially was valued by inner learning.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming era the foreign monk Mahayana, an ascetic of refined understanding, produced many new sutras in the capital; the Shravakabhumi Sutra was especially prized among Buddhist scholars.

sentences.zh: 東夷高句驪國，今治漢之遼東郡。

translations.literal: The Eastern Yi state of Goguryeo—now governing Han's Liaodong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Yi kingdom of Goguryeo now occupied the territory of Han's Liaodong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高句驪王高璉，晉安帝義熙九年，遣長史高翼奉表獻赭白馬。

translations.literal: The King of Goguryeo, Gao Lian—in the ninth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, sent Senior Clerk Gao Yi to present a memorial and offer a sorrel-and-white horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yixi (413), King Gao Lian of Goguryeo sent Senior Clerk Gao Yi with a memorial and tribute of a sorrel-and-white horse.

sentences.zh: 以璉為使持節、都督營州諸軍事、征東將軍、高句驪王、樂浪公。

translations.literal: Lian was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander of all military affairs of Ying Province, General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryeo, and Duke of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Ying Province, General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryeo, and Duke of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，詔曰：「使持節、都督營州諸軍事、征東將軍、高句驪王、樂浪公璉，使持節、督百濟諸軍事、鎮東將軍、百濟王映，並執義海外，遠修貢職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, an edict said: "Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander of all military affairs of Ying Province, General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryeo, Duke of Lelang Lian; Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of all military affairs of Baekje, General Who Pacifies the East, King of Baekje Ying—both uphold righteousness beyond the seas, far maintaining tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, he issued an edict: "Lian, Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Ying Province, General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryeo, and Duke of Lelang, and Ying, Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Baekje, General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Baekje, have both upheld righteousness beyond the seas and faithfully sent tribute from afar.

sentences.zh: 惟新告始，宜荷國休，璉可征東大將軍，映可鎮東大將軍。

translations.literal: At the renewal that announces the beginning, they ought to bear the state's grace—Lian may be made Grand General Who Conquers the East; Ying may be made Grand General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: At this renewal of the dynasty they deserve the state's favor: Lian is promoted to Grand General Who Conquers the East, and Ying to Grand General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 持節、都督、王、公如故。」

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander, King, and Duke as before."
translations.idiomatic: Their titles as Bearer of the Staff, commander, king, and duke remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 三年，加璉散騎常侍，增督平州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the third year, Lian was additionally given Regular Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and his supervision was increased to all military affairs of Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his reign Lian was further appointed Regular Attendant and given additional command over Ping Province.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平二年，璉遣長史馬婁等詣闕獻方物，遣使慰勞之，曰：「皇帝問使持節、散騎常侍、都督營平二州諸軍事、征東大將軍、高句驪王、樂浪公，纂戎東服，庸績繼軌，厥惠既彰，款誠亦著，踰遼越海，納貢本朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping under the Lesser Emperor, Lian sent Senior Clerk Ma Lou and others to the court to present local products; envoys were dispatched to comfort and reward them, saying: "The Emperor inquires of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, Area Commander of all military affairs of Ying and Ping provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryeo, Duke of Lelang: inheriting arms in the eastern domain, meritorious deeds continuing the track—your grace already displayed, sincere devotion also evident, crossing Liaodong and the sea to bring tribute to this court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingping (424), Lian sent Senior Clerk Ma Lou and others to court with local tribute. The emperor dispatched envoys with words of comfort: "The Emperor inquires of Lian, Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, Commander of Ying and Ping provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryeo, and Duke of Lelang: you have inherited your post in the eastern marches and continued your predecessors' service. Your grace is manifest and your loyalty clear, crossing the Liaodong frontier and the sea to bring tribute to our court.

sentences.zh: 朕以不德，忝承鴻緒，永懷先蹤，思覃遺澤。

translations.literal: I, lacking virtue, presumptuously inherit the great succession, forever cherishing the former tracks, thinking to spread the lingering grace.
translations.idiomatic: I, lacking virtue, have undeservedly inherited the great throne. I ever recall the deeds of my predecessors and seek to extend their legacy.

sentences.zh: 今遣謁者朱邵伯、副謁者王邵子等，宣旨慰勞。

translations.literal: Now I send Usher Zhu Shaobo, Assistant Usher Wang Shaozi, and others to proclaim the imperial intent and comfort and reward.
translations.idiomatic: I now send the ushers Zhu Shaobo and Wang Shaozi to convey my message and express my regard.

sentences.zh: 其茂康惠政，永隆厥功，式昭往命，稱朕意焉。」

translations.literal: May you flourish in health, govern with benevolent policy, forever elevate your achievements, and display the former commission—matching my intent."
translations.idiomatic: May you prosper, govern with benevolence, and long uphold your service, fulfilling the charge entrusted to you and my own wishes."

sentences.zh: 先是，鮮卑慕容寶治中山，為索虜所破，東走黃龍。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Xianbei Murong Bao ruled Zhongshan, was broken by the Northern Wei, and fled east to Huanglong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Xianbei ruler Murong Bao had governed Zhongshan until defeated by the Northern Wei and driven east to Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，寶弟熙為其下馮跋所殺，跋自立為主，自號燕王，以其治黃龍城，故謂之黃龍國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi, Bao's younger brother Xi was killed by his subordinate Feng Ba; Ba established himself as lord, styled himself Prince of Yan—because he governed Huanglong city, it was called the Huanglong state.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yixi era (405), Bao's brother Xi was killed by his general Feng Ba, who seized power and styled himself Prince of Yan. Because he ruled from Huanglong city, his realm was called the Huanglong kingdom.

sentences.zh: 跋死，子弘立，屢為索虜所攻，不能下。

translations.literal: When Ba died, his son Hong established [the rule]; [11] repeatedly attacked by the Northern Wei, they could not subdue him.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Ba died, his son Hong succeeded him.[11] The Northern Wei attacked repeatedly but could not bring him down.

sentences.zh: 太祖世，每歲遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: During Emperor Taizu's reign, every year envoys were sent to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Emperor Wen's reign they sent tribute annually.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，賜加除授。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia, bestowal and additional appointment were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia (435) additional titles and appointments were conferred.

sentences.zh: 十五年，復為索虜所攻，弘敗走，奔高驪北豐城，表求迎接。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, again attacked by the Northern Wei, Hong was defeated and fled, running to Goguryeo's Beifeng city, memorializing to request escort and reception.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (438) the Northern Wei attacked again. Hong was defeated and fled to Beifeng city in Goguryeo, where he petitioned the Liu Song court for rescue.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣使王白駒、趙次興迎之，并令高驪料理資遣，璉不欲使弘南，乃遣將孫漱、高仇等襲殺之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu dispatched envoys Wang Baiju and Zhao Cixing to welcome him, and also ordered Goguryeo to arrange supplies and escort—but Lian did not wish Hong to go south, and therefore sent generals Sun Su, Gao Chou, and others to attack and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent Wang Baiju and Zhao Cixing to escort him south and ordered Goguryeo to provide supplies for the journey. Lian, unwilling to let Hong reach the south, sent generals Sun Su and Gao Chou to ambush and kill him.

sentences.zh: 白駒等率所領七千餘人掩討漱等，生禽漱，殺高仇等二人。

translations.literal: Baiju and others led the more than seven thousand men under their command in a surprise attack against Su and the rest; Su was captured alive; Gao Chou and two others were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Baiju led his force of more than seven thousand men in a surprise attack, captured Sun Su alive, and killed Gao Chou and two others.

sentences.zh: 璉以白駒等專殺，遣使執送之，上以遠國，不欲違其意，白駒等下獄，見原。

translations.literal: Lian, because Baiju and others had killed on their own authority, sent envoys to seize and deliver them—the Emperor, because it was a distant state, did not wish to go against their intent; Baiju and others were imprisoned and then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Lian demanded that Wang Baiju and his men be handed over for having killed without authorization. The emperor, not wishing to offend a distant ally, had them imprisoned but then pardoned.

sentences.zh: 璉每歲遣使。

translations.literal: Lian every year sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Lian continued to send envoys every year.

sentences.zh: 十六年，太祖欲北討，詔璉送馬，璉獻馬八百匹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Emperor Taizu wished to campaign north and ordered Lian to send horses—Lian presented eight hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (439), as Emperor Wen prepared a northern campaign, he ordered Lian to supply horses; Lian sent eight hundred.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝建二年，璉遣長史董騰奉表慰國哀再周，幷獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Shizu, Lian sent Senior Clerk Dong Teng to present a memorial comforting [the court] on the second anniversary of national mourning, and also presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian (455), Lian sent Senior Clerk Dong Teng with a memorial of condolence on the second anniversary of the emperor's mourning and with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，又獻肅慎氏楛矢石砮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming, he again presented the Sushen clan's birch-bark arrows and stone arrowheads.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daming (459) he again sent birch arrows and stone arrowheads of Sushen make.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔曰：「使持節、散騎常侍、督平營二州諸軍事、征東大將軍、高句驪王、樂浪公璉，世事忠義，作藩海外，誠係本朝，志剪殘險，通譯沙表，克宣王猷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict said: "Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, Supervisor of all military affairs of Ping and Ying provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryeo, Duke of Lelang Lian: through generations loyal and righteous, serving as frontier beyond the seas, sincerely bound to this court, resolved to cut down remnant peril, communicating through interpreters beyond the sands, able to proclaim the king's plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (463) an edict declared: "Lian, Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, Commander of Ping and Ying provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryeo, and Duke of Lelang, has through generations shown loyalty and righteousness as a frontier prince beyond the seas. Sincerely bound to our court and resolved to destroy our enemies, he communicates across the frontier and faithfully carries out the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 宜加褒進，以旌純節。

translations.literal: He ought to receive increased praise and promotion, to mark pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He deserves further honor to mark his steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 可車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，持節、常侍、都督、王、公如故。」

translations.literal: He may be made General of Chariots and Cavalry, Opener of the Office with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies; Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, Area Commander, King, and Duke as before."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Opener of the Office with the ceremonial rank of the Three Excellencies; his other titles remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始、後廢帝元徽中，貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: During Taishi under Emperor Taizong and Yuanhui under the Later Deposed Emperor, tribute and offerings did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi and Yuanhui eras under Emperors Ming and Houfei, tribute continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 百濟國，本與高驪俱在遼東之東千餘里，其後高驪略有遼東，百濟略有遼西。

translations.literal: The state of Baekje—originally together with Goguryeo lay more than a thousand li east of Liaodong; afterward Goguryeo partially took Liaodong, Baekje partially took Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Baekje originally lay more than a thousand li east of Liaodong, alongside Goguryeo. Later Goguryeo seized part of Liaodong and Baekje part of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 百濟所治，謂之晉平郡晉平縣。

translations.literal: Where Baekje governed was called Jinping Commandery, Jinping County.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje's seat was known as Jinping Commandery, Jinping County.

sentences.zh: 義熙十二年，以百濟王餘映為使持節、都督百濟諸軍事、鎮東將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yixi, Yu Ying, King of Baekje, was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of all military affairs of Baekje, General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yixi (416), Yu Ying, King of Baekje, was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Baekje, General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Baekje.

sentences.zh: [12]高祖踐阼，進號鎮東大將軍。

translations.literal: [12] When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, his title was advanced to Grand General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: [12] When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, Yu Ying was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平二年，映遣長史張威詣闕貢獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping under the Lesser Emperor, Ying sent Senior Clerk Zhang Wei to the court to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingping (424), Ying sent Senior Clerk Zhang Wei to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，太祖詔之曰：「皇帝問使持節、都督百濟諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia, Emperor Taizu addressed him with an edict, saying: "The Emperor inquires of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of all military affairs of Baekje, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, King of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia (425), Emperor Wen addressed him with an edict: "The Emperor sends greetings to Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Baekje, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 累葉忠順，越海効誠，遠王纂戎，聿修先業，慕義既彰，厥懷赤款，浮桴驪水，獻賝執贄，故嗣位方任，以藩東服，勉勗所莅，無墜前蹤。

translations.literal: Through generations loyal and obedient, crossing the sea to show sincerity, a distant king inheriting arms, promptly restoring the former enterprise, admiration for righteousness already manifested, his heart sincere and devoted, floating rafts on the dark waters, presenting tribute and holding gifts—therefore upon succeeding to the throne was given responsibility, as eastern frontier vassal, encouraged in what he governs, not to fall from former tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive reigns your house has shown loyalty and submission, crossing the sea to prove its devotion. You have inherited the throne, taken up arms, and restored your ancestors' enterprise. Your zeal for righteousness is manifest and your heart utterly sincere. You have crossed the waters by raft to bring tribute and gifts. On succeeding to the throne you were entrusted with office as a frontier prince in the east. We urge you to govern well and not fall short of your forebears.

sentences.zh: 今遣兼謁者閭丘恩子、兼副謁者丁敬子等宣旨慰勞稱朕意。」

translations.literal: Now dispatching Concurrent Master of Ceremonies Luqiu Enzi, Concurrent Deputy Master of Ceremonies Ding Jingzi, and others to proclaim the edict, console and reward, speaking My intent."
translations.idiomatic: We are sending the Concurrent Master of Ceremonies Luqiu Enzi and the Concurrent Deputy Master of Ceremonies Ding Jingzi to proclaim this edict, convey our consolation and commendation, and speak on Our behalf."

sentences.zh: 其後每歲遣使奉表，獻方物。

translations.literal: Afterwards each year envoys were sent with memorials, presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter envoys were sent every year with memorials and regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年，百濟王餘毗復修貢職，以映爵號授之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, King Yu Pi of Baekje again restored tribute duties; Ying's noble title was conferred upon him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (430), King Yu Pi of Baekje again resumed tribute. He was granted the titles held by Yu Ying.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，毗上書獻方物，私假臺使馮野夫西河太守，表求易林、式占、腰弩，太祖並與之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Pi submitted a memorial presenting local products; privately through court envoy Feng Yefu, Prefect of Xihe, [he] memorialized requesting the Yilin, Shizhan, and waist crossbows; Emperor Taizu granted all.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (449), Pi submitted a memorial with regional gifts. Through the court envoy Feng Yefu, prefect of Xihe, he privately petitioned for copies of the Yilin, Shizhan, and waist crossbows; Emperor Wen granted everything requested.

sentences.zh: 毗死，子慶代立。

translations.literal: Pi died; his son Qing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi died, his son Qing succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明元年，遣使求除授，詔許。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming under Emperor Shizu, [Baekje] sent envoys requesting official appointments; an edict granted [them].
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming (457), Baekje sent envoys asking for formal appointments, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 二年，慶遣使上表曰：「臣國累葉，偏受殊恩，文武良輔，世蒙朝爵。

translations.literal: In the second year, Qing sent envoys with a memorial saying: "My state through generations has especially received extraordinary grace; civil and military worthy assistants through generations have received court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Qing sent envoys with a memorial stating: "Through many reigns my kingdom has enjoyed exceptional favor. Worthy ministers, civil and military alike, have generation after generation received ranks from Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 行冠軍將軍右賢王餘紀等十一人，忠勤宜在顯進，伏願垂愍，並聽賜除。」

translations.literal: Acting General Who Conquers the Champions Right Worthy King Yu Ji and eleven others—loyalty and diligence deserve prominent promotion; I humbly wish you would show compassion and all be granted appointments."
translations.idiomatic: Acting General Who Conquers the Champions and Right Worthy King Yu Ji and eleven others have served with such loyalty and diligence that they merit promotion. I humbly ask Your Majesty to show them compassion and grant them appointments.

sentences.zh: 仍以行冠軍將軍右賢王餘紀為冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Acting General Who Conquers the Champions Right Worthy King Yu Ji was made General Who Conquers the Champions.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ji, Acting General Who Conquers the Champions and Right Worthy King, was appointed General Who Conquers the Champions.

sentences.zh: 以行征虜將軍左賢王餘昆、行征虜將軍餘暈並為征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Acting General Who Conquers Barbarians Left Worthy King Yu Kun and Acting General Who Conquers Barbarians Yu Yun were both made Generals Who Conquer Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kun, Acting General Who Conquers Barbarians and Left Worthy King, and Yu Yun, Acting General Who Conquers Barbarians, were both promoted to full Generals Who Conquer Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 以行輔國將軍餘都、餘乂並為輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Acting General Who Assists the State Yu Du and Yu Yi were both made Generals Who Assist the State.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Du and Yu Yi, both Acting Generals Who Assist the State, were appointed full Generals Who Assist the State.

sentences.zh: 以行龍驤將軍沐衿、餘爵並為龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Acting General of the Flying Dragon Mu Jin and Yu Jue were both made Generals of the Flying Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Jin and Yu Jue, both Acting Generals of the Flying Dragon, were appointed full Generals of the Flying Dragon.

sentences.zh: 以行寧朔將軍餘流、麋貴並為寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: Acting General Who Pacifies the North Yu Liu and Mi Gui were both made Generals Who Pacify the North.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liu and Mi Gui, both Acting Generals Who Pacify the North, were appointed full Generals Who Pacify the North.

sentences.zh: 以行建武將軍于西、餘婁並為建武將軍。

translations.literal: Acting General Who Establishes Might Yu Xi and Yu Lou were both made Generals Who Establish Might.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi and Yu Lou, both Acting Generals Who Establish Might, were appointed full Generals Who Establish Might.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始七年，又遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi under Emperor Taizong, [Baekje] again sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taishi (471), during the reign of Emperor Ming, Baekje again sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 倭國在高驪東南大海中，世修貢職。

translations.literal: The state of Wa lies in the great sea southeast of Goguryeo; through generations it maintained tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Wa lay in the open sea southeast of Goguryeo and for generations faithfully paid tribute.

sentences.zh: 高祖永初二年，詔曰：「倭讚萬里修貢，遠誠宜甄，可賜除授。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu under Emperor Gaozu, an edict said: "King San of Wa, ten thousand li maintaining tribute—distant sincerity ought to be distinguished; may grant appointments."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu (421), Emperor Gaozu issued an edict: "King San of Wa sends tribute from ten thousand li away. Such distant sincerity deserves recognition; let him be granted titles and office."

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉二年，讚又遣司馬曹達奉表獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu, San again sent Marshal Cao Da to present a memorial and offer local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia (425), San again sent the marshal Cao Da with a memorial and regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 讚死，弟珍立，遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: San died; his younger brother Zhen succeeded; sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When San died, his younger brother Zhen succeeded and sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 自稱使持節、都督倭百濟新羅任那秦韓慕韓六國諸軍事、安東大將軍、倭國王。

translations.literal: He styled himself Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of all military affairs of the six states Wa, Baekje, Silla, Imna, Qinhan, and Mohan, General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander of the Six States of Wa, Baekje, Silla, Imna, Qinhan, and Mohan, General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa.

sentences.zh: 表求除正，詔除安東將軍、倭國王。

translations.literal: Memorial requesting formal appointment; edict appointed General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne asking for formal appointment, and the court named him General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa.

sentences.zh: 珍又求除正倭隋等十三人平西、征虜、冠軍、輔國將軍號，詔並聽。

translations.literal: Zhen again requested formal appointment for Wa Sui and twelve others—Generals Who Pacify the West, Who Conquer Barbarians, Who Conquer the Champions, and Who Assist the State; edict granted all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen again asked that thirteen men including Wa Sui be formally appointed to the ranks of General Who Pacifies the West, General Who Conquers Barbarians, General Who Conquers the Champions, and General Who Assists the State; the court granted all the requests.

sentences.zh: 二十年，倭國王濟遣使奉獻，復以為安東將軍、倭國王。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, King Ji of Wa sent envoys with tribute; again appointed General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (443), King Ji of Wa sent envoys with tribute and was again confirmed as General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，加使持節、都督倭新羅任那加羅秦韓慕韓六國諸軍事，安東將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, added Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of all military affairs of the six states Wa, Silla, Imna, Kara, Qinhan, and Mohan; General Who Pacifies the East as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (451) he was further granted the titles Bearer of the Staff and Commander of the Six States of Wa, Silla, Imna, Kara, Qinhan, and Mohan; his title of General Who Pacifies the East remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 并除所上二十三人軍、郡。

translations.literal: And appointed the twenty-three military and prefectural [offices] submitted on the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-three military and prefectural appointments he had listed were also granted.

sentences.zh: 濟死，世子興遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: Ji died; the crown prince Xing sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji died, the crown prince Xing sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明六年，詔曰：「倭王世子興，奕世載忠，作藩外海，稟化寧境，恭修貢職。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daming under Emperor Shizu, an edict said: "Crown Prince Xing of Wa—generations loading loyalty, serving as frontier beyond the seas, receiving transformation pacifying the realm, respectfully maintaining tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daming (462), Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict: "Crown Prince Xing of Wa has borne loyalty through many reigns, guarded the frontier beyond the seas, received our civilization and kept his realm at peace, and faithfully maintained tribute.

sentences.zh: 新嗣邊業，宜授爵號，可安東將軍、倭國王。」

translations.literal: Newly succeeding the frontier enterprise, ought to grant noble title: may be General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa."
translations.idiomatic: Having newly inherited this frontier charge, he should receive rank and title: let him be General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa."

sentences.zh: 興死，弟武立，自稱使持節、都督倭百濟新羅任那加羅秦韓慕韓七國諸軍事、安東大將軍、倭國王。

translations.literal: Xing died; his younger brother Wu succeeded; styled himself Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of all military affairs of the seven states Wa, Baekje, Silla, Imna, Kara, Qinhan, and Mohan, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing died, his younger brother Wu succeeded and styled himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander of the Seven States of Wa, Baekje, Silla, Imna, Kara, Qinhan, and Mohan, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明二年，遣使上表曰：「封國偏遠，作藩于外，自昔祖禰，躬擐甲冑，跋涉山川，不遑寧處。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming under Emperor Shundi, [Wu] sent envoys with a memorial saying: "My sealed state is remote and distant, serving as frontier without; from old my ancestors, personally bearing armor and helmet, traversing mountains and rivers, with no leisure for rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming (478), Wu sent envoys with a memorial stating: "My kingdom lies far away, a frontier realm beyond the seas. From our earliest ancestors we have worn armor and marched through mountains and rivers without rest.

sentences.zh: 東征毛人五十五國，西服眾夷六十六國，渡平海北九十五國，王道融泰，廓土遐畿，累葉朝宗，不愆于歲。

translations.literal: Eastward subjugating the hairy people of fifty-five states, westward submitting the various Yi of sixty-six states, crossing and pacifying ninety-five states north of the sea—the royal way harmonious and great, broadening the realm to distant frontiers; generation after generation paying court homage, never missing a year.
translations.idiomatic: We have conquered fifty-five hairy-peoples' states to the east and brought sixty-six Yi domains of the west to submission; we have crossed the sea and pacified ninety-five states to the north. The royal way flourishes and our territory reaches the distant marches. Generation after generation we have paid homage at court, never missing a year.

sentences.zh: 臣雖下愚，忝胤先緒，驅率所統，歸崇天極，道逕百濟，[13]裝治船舫，而句驪無道，圖欲見吞，掠抄邊隸，虔劉不已，每致稽滯，以失良風。

translations.literal: Although I am lowly and foolish, I humbly inherit my ancestors' line; driving and leading those under my command, I turn toward revering the celestial pole. The route passes through Baekje; [13] ships are fitted out—yet Goguryeo is without the Way and intends to swallow us, plundering border subjects, slaughtering without cease, ever causing delay and hindrance, thereby losing fine custom.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am unworthy, I have inherited my forebears' charge and lead my people in homage to the celestial throne. Our route lies through Baekje; [13] we have prepared ships for the voyage. But Goguryeo, devoid of justice, seeks to swallow us whole. It raids our border people and slaughters without end, delaying our embassies again and again and breaking the good custom of tribute.

sentences.zh: 雖曰進路，或通或不。

translations.literal: Although called a route of advance, at times it passes and at times it does not.
translations.idiomatic: Though we call it the road to court, sometimes it is open and sometimes barred.

sentences.zh: 臣亡考濟實忿寇讎，壅塞天路，控弦百萬，義聲感激，方欲大舉，奄喪父兄，使垂成之功，不獲一簣。

translations.literal: My late father Ji truly resented the enemy and foe, blocking the heavenly route; controlling a million bowstrings, righteous voices stirred, about to launch a great campaign—suddenly losing father and elder brother, making the nearly completed enterprise fail to gain one basket [of earth].
translations.idiomatic: My late father Ji burned with hatred for this enemy, who had choked off the road to the Son of Heaven. With a million archers at his call and his righteous fury roused, he was on the verge of a great campaign when death suddenly took him and his brother—so the work nearly done was lost for want of one last basket of earth.

sentences.zh: 居在諒闇，不動兵甲，是以偃息未捷。

translations.literal: Dwelling in mourning obscurity, not moving arms and armor—therefore ceasing and resting, success not yet achieved.
translations.idiomatic: I remain in mourning and have not taken up arms; hence we have paused, and victory is still unrealized.

sentences.zh: 至今欲練甲治兵，申父兄之志，義士虎賁，文武效功，白刃交前，亦所不顧。

translations.literal: Until now I wish to drill armor and regulate troops, declaring father and elder brother's intent; righteous warriors and tiger guards, civil and military rendering achievement—before crossed blades I also do not look back.
translations.idiomatic: But now I mean to train armor and marshal troops to fulfill my father and brother's purpose. My loyal warriors, civil and military alike, will serve to the death; even with blades before them they will not turn back.

sentences.zh: 若以帝德覆載，摧此強敵，克靖方難，無替前功。

translations.literal: If by the Emperor's virtue covering and bearing all, this strong enemy is overthrown, difficulty in the regions is pacified, not failing the former achievement.
translations.idiomatic: If by Your Majesty's all-encompassing virtue this mighty foe can be crushed and the frontier troubles settled, we shall not fall short of the achievements of those who came before us.

sentences.zh: 竊自假開府儀同三司，其餘咸各假授，[14]以勸忠節。」

translations.literal: I presumptuously self-appoint Acting Opener of the Office with the Same Ceremonials as the Three Excellencies; the rest I likewise grant acting appointments, [14] to encourage loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: I have taken upon myself the acting rank of Opener of the Office with the Ceremonial of the Three Excellencies, and have provisionally granted the rest their titles [14] to reward loyalty and steadfast service."

sentences.zh: 詔除武使持節、都督倭新羅任那加羅秦韓慕韓六國諸軍事、安東大將軍、倭王。

translations.literal: Edict appointed Wu Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of all military affairs of the six states Wa, Silla, Imna, Kara, Qinhan, and Mohan, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: An edict confirmed Wu as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of the Six States of Wa, Silla, Imna, Kara, Qinhan, and Mohan, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍州蠻，槃瓠之後也。

translations.literal: The barbarians of Jing and Yong provinces are descendants of Pan Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians of Jing and Yong provinces were descendants of Pan Hu.

sentences.zh: 分建種落，布在諸郡縣。

translations.literal: [They] separately established tribes and clans, distributed among various commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Their clans were divided and settled across many commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 荊州置南蠻，雍州置寧蠻校尉以領之。

translations.literal: Jing Province established the Southern Barbarians [office]; Yong Province established the Pacifying Barbarians Commandant to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province maintained a Southern Barbarians office; Yong Province maintained a Pacifying Barbarians Commandant to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，罷南蠻併大府，而寧蠻如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizu, the Southern Barbarians [office] was abolished and merged into the Great Prefecture; the Pacifying Barbarians [office] remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Xiaowu the Southern Barbarians office was abolished and merged into the chief prefecture, while the Pacifying Barbarians command remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 蠻民順附者，一戶輸穀數斛，其餘無雜調，而宋民賦役嚴苦，貧者不復堪命，多逃亡入蠻。

translations.literal: Barbarian people who submitted in obedience—each household paid several hu of grain; the rest had no miscellaneous levies; yet Song commoners' taxes and corvée were harsh and bitter, the poor no longer able to bear the charge, many fleeing and entering among the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians who submitted paid only a few hu of grain per household and owed no other levies; by contrast Song subjects faced crushing taxes and corvée. The poor could no longer endure it, and many fled into barbarian territory.

sentences.zh: 蠻無傜役，強者又不供官稅，結黨連羣，動有數百千人，州郡力弱，則起為盜賊，種類稍多，戶口不可知也。

translations.literal: Barbarians had no corvée and forced labor; the strong also did not supply official grain taxes, forming factions and linking in groups—when moving, there were often several hundred or thousand men; when prefectures and commanderies were weak in force, they rose as bandits and robbers; as types gradually increased, registered households could not be known.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians owed no corvée, and their strong men did not pay official grain tax either. They formed bands of hundreds or thousands. Where provincial and commandery forces were weak they turned to banditry. Their numbers grew until no one could say how many households they comprised.

sentences.zh: 所在多深險，居武陵者有雄谿、樠谿、辰谿、酉谿、舞谿，[15]謂之五谿蠻。

translations.literal: Where they dwelled was mostly deep and perilous; those dwelling in Wuling had Xiong Stream, Man Stream, Chen Stream, You Stream, and Wu Stream—[15] called the Five Stream Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: They lived mostly in rugged, inaccessible country. Those in Wuling along the Xiong, Man, Chen, You, and Wu streams [15] were called the Five Stream Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 而宜都、天門、巴東、建平、江北諸郡蠻，所居皆深山重阻，人跡罕至焉。

translations.literal: The barbarians of Yidu, Tianmen, Badong, Jianping, and the north-of-the-river commanderies of the region—they dwelled all in deep mountains and heavy barriers, human tracks rarely reaching there.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians in Yidu, Tianmen, Badong, Jianping, and the Han River north country likewise lived in deep mountains behind steep passes, where hardly any traveler went.

sentences.zh: 前世以來，屢為民患。

translations.literal: From former ages onward, repeatedly becoming harm to the people.
translations.idiomatic: From earlier dynasties they had repeatedly troubled the population.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平二年，宜都蠻帥石寧等一百二十三人詣闕上獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping under the Lesser Emperor, Yidu barbarian chieftain Shi Ning and one hundred twenty-three others came to the court to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingping (424), the Yidu barbarian chieftain Shi Ning and one hundred twenty-three others came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉六年，建平蠻張雍之等五十人，七年，宜都蠻田生等一百一十三人，並詣闕獻見。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu, Jianping barbarian Zhang Yongzhi and fifty others; in the seventh year, Yidu barbarian Tian Sheng and one hundred thirteen others—all came to the court and were received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanjia (429), fifty Jianping barbarians led by Zhang Yongzhi; in the seventh year, one hundred thirteen Yidu barbarians led by Tian Sheng—all came to court for audience.

sentences.zh: 其後沔中蠻大動，行旅殆絕。

translations.literal: Afterwards the barbarians of the Mian region greatly stirred; travelers were nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Mian River barbarians rose in force and travel along the route nearly ceased.

sentences.zh: 天門漊中令宗矯之傜賦過重，蠻不堪命。

translations.literal: Zong Jiaozhi, magistrate of Liao Middle in Tianmen, imposed corvée and levies too heavily; [16] the barbarians could not bear the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Jiaozhi, magistrate of Liao Middle in Tianmen, imposed corvée and levies that were far too heavy; [16] the barbarians could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 十八年，蠻田向求等為寇，破漊中，虜略百姓。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, barbarians Tian Xiangqiu and others raided, broke Liao Middle, captured and plundered the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (441) the barbarians Tian Xiangqiu and others rebelled, overran Liao Middle, and carried off the populace.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史衡陽王義季遣行參軍曹孫念討破之，獲生口五百餘人，免矯之官。

translations.literal: Jingzhou Inspector Prince of Hengyang Yiji dispatched Acting Retainer Cao Sunnian to attack and defeat them, capturing more than five hundred living captives; Jiaozhi was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou inspector the Prince of Hengyang, Yiji, sent the acting retainer Cao Sunnian to attack and rout them, taking more than five hundred captives alive. Jiaozhi was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，南郡臨沮當陽蠻反，縛臨沮令傅僧驥。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Nan Commandery Linju Dangyang barbarians rebelled, bound Linju Magistrate Fu Songji.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (447), the Linju and Dangyang barbarians of Nan Commandery rebelled and seized the Linju magistrate Fu Songji.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史南譙王義宣遣中兵參軍王諶討破之。

translations.literal: Jingzhou Inspector Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan dispatched Central Army Retainer Wang Chen to attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou inspector the Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan, sent the central army retainer Wang Chen to attack and defeat them.

sentences.zh: 先是，雍州刺史劉道產善撫諸蠻，前後不附官者，莫不順服，皆引出平土，多緣沔為居。

translations.literal: Before this, Yongzhou Inspector Liu Daochan was skilled at soothing the various barbarians; those who before had not attached to the government, none did not submit in obedience, all being led out to level land, mostly dwelling along the Mian as residence.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yongzhou inspector Liu Daochan had been adept at winning over the barbarians. Those who had refused submission all came to obey, and he resettled many along level ground near the Mian River.

sentences.zh: 及道產亡，蠻又反叛。

translations.literal: When Daochan died, the barbarians again rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Daochan died the barbarians rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 及世祖出為雍州，羣蠻斷道，擊大破之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu went out as Yongzhou [Inspector], the massed barbarians blocked the roads; he attacked and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiaowu took up his post in Yongzhou, barbarian bands cut the roads; he attacked and routed them.

sentences.zh: 臺遣軍主沈慶之連年討蠻，所向皆平殄，事在慶之傳。

translations.literal: The court dispatched Army Commander Shen Qingzhi for successive years to campaign against barbarians; wherever he went all were pacified and exterminated—the matter is in Qingzhi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent the army commander Shen Qingzhi against them year after year; wherever he marched they were suppressed. The campaigns are recorded in Qingzhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月，龍山雉水蠻寇抄湼陽縣，南陽太守朱曇韶遣軍討之，失利，殺傷三百餘人，曇韶又遣二千人係之，蠻乃散走。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year, Long Mountain Zhishui barbarians raided and plundered Niyang County; Nanyang Prefect Zhu Tanshao dispatched troops to attack them, suffered defeat, killed and wounded more than three hundred men; Tanshao again sent two thousand men to pursue them—the barbarians then scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year (451), Long Mountain and Zhishui barbarians raided Niyang County. Nanyang prefect Zhu Tanshao sent troops against them but was defeated, with more than three hundred killed or wounded. Tanshao then sent two thousand men in pursuit, and the barbarians broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 是歲，滍水諸蠻因險為寇，雍州刺史隨王誕遣使說之曰：「頃威懷所被，覃自遐遠，順化者寵祿，逆命者無遺，此亦爾所知也。

translations.literal: That year, various barbarians of the Zhi waters relied on peril to raid; Yongzhou Inspector Prince of Sui Wang Dan dispatched envoys to address them, saying: "Recently where might and kindness extended, beneficence reached even the distant; those who yielded to transformation received favor and emolument, those who resisted command left nothing behind—this too you know.
translations.idiomatic: That same year barbarians along the Zhi River exploited the terrain to raid. Yongzhou inspector the Prince of Sui, Dan, sent envoys to address them: "You have seen how the Emperor's favor reaches even the farthest lands. Those who submit receive reward; those who resist are destroyed without remainder.

sentences.zh: 聖朝今普天肆眚，許以自新，便宜各還舊居，安堵復業，改過革心，於是乎始。」

translations.literal: The Sagely Court now universally extends amnesty throughout heaven, permitting self-renewal; it is fitting that each return to former dwelling, peaceably resettling and resuming enterprise; reforming errors and renewing the heart—therein lies the beginning."
translations.idiomatic: The court now grants a general amnesty and offers renewal. Return to your old homes, live in peace, and resume your livelihoods. Let this be the moment you change your ways."

sentences.zh: 先是，蠻帥魯奴子擄龍山，屢為邊患。

translations.literal: Before this, barbarian chieftain Lu Nuzi captured Long Mountain and repeatedly was a border affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the barbarian chieftain Lu Nuzi had seized Long Mountain and repeatedly troubled the frontier.

sentences.zh: 魯軌在長社，奴子歸之，軌言於虜主，以為四山王。

translations.literal: Lu Gui was at Changshe; Nuzi returned to him; Gui spoke to the Northern lord, and [Nuzi] was made Prince of Four Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gui was at Changshe; Nuzi went over to him. Gui spoke to the Northern Wei ruler, and Nuzi was made Prince of the Four Mountains.

sentences.zh: 軌子爽歸國，奴子亦求內附，隨王誕又遣軍討沔北諸蠻，襲濁山、如口、蜀松三柴，剋之，又圍升錢、柏義諸柴，[17]蠻悉力距戰。

translations.literal: Gui's son Shuang returned to the [Song] state; Nuzi also sought internal attachment; Prince of Sui Wang Dan again dispatched troops to campaign against the north-of-the-Mian barbarians, raiding the three stockades Zhuo Mountain, Rukou, and Shusong—taking them; also besieged the stockades Shengqian, Baiyi, and others; [17] the barbarians all exerted strength to resist battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui's son Shuang returned to Song service, Nuzi also sought to submit. The Prince of Sui again sent troops against the barbarians north of the Mian, storming the stockades at Zhuo Mountain, Rukou, and Shusong and then besieging Shengqian, Baiyi, and others. [17] The barbarians resisted with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 軍以具裝馬夾射，大破之，斬首二百級，獲生蠻千口，牛馬八十頭。

translations.literal: The army with fully armored horses shot from both sides, greatly defeating them—beheading two hundred levels, capturing one thousand living barbarians, eighty head of cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Song cavalry in full armor flanked them with bowshot and broke them completely, taking two hundred heads, a thousand captives, and eighty head of cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明中，建平蠻向光侯寇暴峽川，巴東太守王濟、荊州刺史朱修之遣軍討之，光侯走清江。

translations.literal: During Daming under Emperor Shizu, Jianping barbarian Xiang Guanghou raided and ravaged Xia River; Badong Prefect Wang Ji, Jingzhou Inspector Zhu Xiuzhi dispatched troops to attack him; Guanghou fled to Qing River.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming era, the Jianping barbarian chieftain Xiang Guanghou ravaged the Xia River country. Badong prefect Wang Ji and Jingzhou inspector Zhu Xiuzhi sent troops against him, and Guanghou fled to the Qing River.

sentences.zh: 清江去巴東千餘里。

translations.literal: Qing River is more than a thousand li from Badong.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing River lay more than a thousand li from Badong.

sentences.zh: 時巴東、建平、宜都、天門四郡蠻為寇，諸郡民戶流散，百不存一，太宗、順帝世尤甚，雖遣攻伐，終不能禁，荊州為之虛敝。

translations.literal: At the time barbarians of the four commanderies Badong, Jianping, Yidu, and Tianmen were raiding; registered households of the various commanderies scattered and fled—not one in a hundred remaining; under Emperor Taizong and Emperor Shundi it was especially severe; although troops were sent to attack, ultimately they could not be restrained; Jing Province for this was emptied and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time barbarians in Badong, Jianping, Yidu, and Tianmen were raiding, and registered households fled until barely one in a hundred remained. The devastation was worst under Emperors Ming and Shun. Campaign after campaign failed to stop them, and Jing Province was left drained and ruined.

sentences.zh: 大明中，桂陽蠻反，殺荔令晏珍之，臨賀蠻反，殺開建令邢伯兒，[18]振武將軍蕭沖之討之，獲少費多，抵罪。

translations.literal: During Daming, Guiyang barbarians rebelled, killed Li Magistrate Yan Zhenzhi; Linhe barbarians rebelled, killed Kaijian Magistrate Xing Bo'er; [18] General Who Strengthens the Martial Xiao Chongzhi attacked them—capturing few while spending much; punished by offense.
translations.idiomatic: During Daming the Guiyang barbarians rebelled and killed the Li magistrate Yan Zhenzhi; the Linhe barbarians rebelled and killed the Kaijian magistrate Xing Bo'er. [18] General Who Strengthens Martial Xiao Chongzhi was sent against them but took few captives at great cost and was punished.

sentences.zh: 豫州蠻，廩君後也。

translations.literal: Yuzhou barbarians are descendants of Lord Lin.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians of Yuzhou were descendants of Lord Lin.

sentences.zh: 盤瓠及廩君事，並具前史。

translations.literal: The matters of Pan Hu and Lord Lin are fully treated in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: The stories of Pan Hu and Lord Lin are recorded in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 西陽有巴水、蘄水、希水、赤亭水、西歸水，謂之五水蠻，所在並深岨，種落熾盛，歷世為盜賊。

translations.literal: Xiyang had Ba Water, Qi Water, Xi Water, Chiting Water, and Xigui Water—called the Five Water Barbarians; where they dwelled was all deep ravines; tribes flourished greatly; through ages they were bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiyang the Ba, Qi, Xi, Chiting, and Xigui rivers marked the territory of the Five Water Barbarians. They lived in steep ravines, their clans flourished, and for generations they raided as bandits.

sentences.zh: 北接淮、汝，南極江、漢，地方數千里。

translations.literal: North joining Huai and Ru, south reaching the Yangzi and Han, the region several thousand li in extent.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands stretched from the Huai and Ru in the north to the Yangzi and Han in the south, covering several thousand li.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十八年，西陽蠻殺南川令劉臺，并其家口。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia, Xiyang barbarians killed Nanchuan Magistrate Liu Tai and also his household.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia (451), Xiyang barbarians killed Nanchuan magistrate Liu Tai along with his entire household.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，新蔡蠻二千餘人破大雷戍，略公私船舫，悉引入湖。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, more than two thousand Xincai barbarians broke Great Lei garrison, plundered public and private boats and ships, all leading them into the lake.
translations.idiomatic: The next year more than two thousand Xincai barbarians overran Great Lei garrison, seized public and private vessels, and carried them all into the lake.

sentences.zh: 有亡命司馬黑石在蠻中，共為寇盜。
