translations.literal: There was the fugitive Sima Heishi among the barbarians; together they were raiding bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Among the barbarians was the fugitive Sima Heishi, and together they plundered as bandits.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣太子步兵校尉沈慶之率江、荊、雍、豫諸州軍討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu dispatched Crown Prince Infantry Commandant Shen Qingzhi leading armies of Jiang, Jing, Yong, and Yu provinces to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent the crown prince's infantry commandant Shen Qingzhi at the head of armies from Jiang, Jing, Yong, and Yuzhou to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明四年，又遣慶之討西陽蠻，大剋獲而反。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming under Emperor Shizu, again dispatched Qingzhi to attack Xiyang barbarians; greatly defeating and capturing, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming (460), Emperor Xiaowu again sent Qingzhi against the Xiyang barbarians. He won a great victory and returned.

sentences.zh: 司馬黑石徒黨三人，其一人名智，黑石號曰「太公」，以為謀主；

translations.literal: Sima Heishi's follower faction numbered three men; one man named Zhi; Heishi was styled "Grand Duke" and served as strategist;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Heishi had three chief followers. One named Zhi; Heishi was called "Grand Duke" and served as their strategist.

sentences.zh: 一人名安陽，號譙王；

translations.literal: one man named Anyang, styled Prince of Qiao;
translations.idiomatic: One named Anyang, who styled himself Prince of Qiao;

sentences.zh: 一人名續之，號梁王。

translations.literal: one man named Xuzhi, styled Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: and one named Xuzhi, who styled himself Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 蠻文小羅等討禽續之，[19]為蠻世財所篡，小羅等相率斬世財父子六人。

translations.literal: Barbarian chief Wen Xiaoluo and others attacked and captured Xuzhi; [19] was usurped by barbarian Shi Caifu; Xiaoluo and others together beheaded Caifu, father and son, six men.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian leader Wen Xiaoluo and others captured Xuzhi. [19] Shi Caifu, a barbarian chieftain, then seized control; Xiaoluo and the others in turn killed Caifu and five members of his family—six men in all.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史王玄謨遣殿中將軍郭元封慰勞諸蠻，使縛送亡命，蠻乃執智黑石、安陽二人送詣玄謨，[20]世祖使於壽陽斬之。

translations.literal: Yuzhou Inspector Wang Xuanmo dispatched Palace Gentlemen-Official Guo Yuanfeng to console and reward the various barbarians, ordering them to bind and send fugitives; the barbarians then seized Zhi, Heishi, and Anyang and sent them to Xuanmo; [20] Emperor Shizu had them beheaded at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou inspector Wang Xuanmo sent the palace gentleman Guo Yuanfeng to reassure the barbarians and order them to deliver the fugitives. They bound Zhi, Heishi, and Anyang and sent them to Xuanmo. [20] Emperor Xiaowu had them executed at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：漢世西譯遐通，兼途累萬，跨頭痛之山，越繩度之險，生行死徑，身往魂歸。

translations.literal: The Historian says: In Han times the western interpreters reached afar, combined routes tens of thousands [of li]; crossing Headache Mountain, passing the Rope-Crossing peril—living going, dying the path, body going soul returning.
translations.idiomatic: The Historian remarks: In Han times interpreters from the west traveled routes tens of thousands of li long, crossing Headache Mountain and the rope bridges of the deep gorges—journeys on which many set out alive and were brought back only as ashes.

sentences.zh: 晉氏南移，河、隴敻隔，戎夷梗路，外域天斷。

translations.literal: When the Jin house moved south, the Yellow and Long [River region] were far separated; Rong and Yi blocked the roads; outer domains heaven-cut-off.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin court moved south, the Yellow and Long River country lay beyond reach; barbarians choked the roads, and the outer world seemed severed from heaven.

sentences.zh: 若夫大秦、天竺，迥出西溟，二漢銜役，特艱斯路，而商貨所資，或出交部，汎海陵波，因風遠至。

translations.literal: As for Great Qin and Tianzhu, far emerging from the western sea, two Han linked service—especially difficult this road; yet what merchant goods relied on sometimes came from Jiaozhi, floating the sea over waves, following wind to reach far.
translations.idiomatic: Great Qin and India lay far beyond the western sea. Even in Han times envoys found the route arduous; yet goods still came, sometimes through Jiaozhi, borne on ships across open sea and carried far by the monsoon winds.

sentences.zh: 又重峻參差，氏眾非一，殊名詭號，種別類殊，山琛水寶，由茲自出，通犀翠羽之珍，蛇珠火布之異，千名萬品，並世主之所虛心，故舟舶繼路，商使交屬。

translations.literal: Also heavy peaks uneven, clans multitude not one; strange names deceitful titles, types and categories different; mountain treasures water gems thereby from here emerge—unicorn horn, kingfisher feather rarities; snake pearl, fire cloth strangenesses; a thousand names ten thousand grades—all what the age's lord empty-heartedly sought; therefore boat ships continued on the road, merchant envoys interlinked.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond them rose countless rugged peaks and innumerable peoples under strange names and titles. Mountain treasures and river jewels flowed from those lands—rhinoceros horn, kingfisher plumes, snake pearls, and fire cloth among marvels beyond counting. Every sage ruler coveted them, and so ships sailed in endless succession and merchant envoys came one after another.

sentences.zh: 太祖以南琛不至，遠命師旅，泉浦之捷，威震滄溟，未名之寶，入充府實。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu because southern treasure did not arrive, far dispatched armies and brigades—the Quanpu victory, might shaking the blue sea; unnamed treasures entered filling the treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: When southern tribute failed to arrive, Emperor Wen dispatched armies far abroad. The victory at Quanpu shook the eastern seas, and unknown treasures filled the imperial stores.

sentences.zh: 夫四夷孔熾，患深自古，蠻、僰殊雜，種眾特繁，依深傍岨，充積畿甸，咫尺華氓，易興狡毒，略財據土，歲月滋深。

translations.literal: The four Yi greatly flourishing, calamity deep from antiquity; Man and Bo exceptionally mixed, types multitudinous especially numerous; relying on depth beside peaks, filling accumulated capital districts; a hand's breadth from Hua commoners—easily raising crafty poison; plundering wealth seizing land, months and years increasingly deep.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier peoples have always been a deep affliction. The Man and Bo were especially numerous, clinging to mountain fastnesses near the capital itself. Living cheek by jowl with Chinese subjects, they easily turned vicious; year by year they plundered and seized territory.

sentences.zh: 自元嘉將半，寇慝彌廣，遂盤結數州，搖亂邦邑。

translations.literal: From Yuanjia nearing the half, bandit evil increasingly broad, then coiling and binding several provinces, shaking and disturbing state towns.
translations.idiomatic: From the middle of the Yuanjia era rebellion spread ever wider until it ensnared whole provinces and unsettled the realm.

sentences.zh: 於是命將出師，恣行誅討，自江漢以北，廬江以南，搜山盪谷，窮兵罄武，繫頸囚俘，蓋以數百萬計。

translations.literal: Thereupon commanding generals to lead armies out, willfully conducting execution and punishment—from north of the Jiang and Han to south of Mount Lu and the river, searching mountains and sweeping valleys, exhausting troops and depleting martial power—neck-bound prisoner captives perhaps numbering in the millions.
translations.idiomatic: Then generals were sent forth to kill without restraint. From the country north of the Han and Yangzi to that south of Mount Lu they scourged mountains and valleys, exhausting armies and prisoners by the millions.

sentences.zh: 至於孩年耋齒，執訊所遺，將卒申好殺之憤，干戈窮酸慘之用，雖云積怨，為報亦甚。

translations.literal: Reaching infant years and hoary tooth, those captured alive in interrogation, remaining soldiers declaring fondness for killing's anger, spears and halberds exhausting bitter cruelty's employment—although called accumulated resentment, the repayment also was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Captives included children and the very old. Soldiers indulged their thirst for blood until war's cruelty was spent. It was said to settle old scores—but the retribution was appalling.

sentences.zh: 張奐所云「流血于野，傷和致災。」

translations.literal: What Zhang Huan said, "blood flowing in the wild, wounding harmony bringing calamity."
translations.idiomatic: As Zhang Huan said, "Blood flows across the fields; harmony is wounded and disaster follows."

sentences.zh: 斯固仁者之言矣。

translations.literal: This indeed is the statement of the benevolent man.
translations.idiomatic: That is truly the word of a humane ruler.
